citation: Page 59 (Book Page): [Wound is generally linear or spindle shaped... shows clean cut margins, sharp angles and smooth walls.] Page 57 (Book Page): [Main characteristics of a lacerated wound are varied shapes with irregular margins, ill defined angles and walls that have bridging tissue tags]

category: Classify injuries on the basis of causative weapons
front: Q: Describe the specific weapon-target relationship required to produce a 'split' or 'crush' laceration.
back: It occurs where skin is compressed between a blunt weapon and an underlying bone (e.g., scalp, chin). The sudden pressure splits the skin and underlying tissues, sometimes mimicking an incised wound.
citation: Page 57 (Book Page): [Split laceration occurs on scalp, forehead, chin or any other part of the body where skin is firmly supported by underlying bone. Sudden compression of the skin and other tissues between the weapon and the underlying bone split them.]

category: Classify injuries on the basis of causative weapons
front: Q: Which two physics-based factors in a weapon primarily control the resulting injury's appearance?
back:
• Weight of the weapon.
• Velocity of the weapon.
Velocity is critical as kinetic energy (K.E.=1/2mv²) determines the magnitude of tissue destruction.
citation: Page 53 (Book Page): [Weight and velocity of weapon and their sum-total control and determine appearance of the wound. Velocity has kinetic energy, which is calculated by formula, K.E.=1/2mv2.]

category: Classify injuries on the basis of causative weapons
front: Q: Classify chemical weapons (corrosives) based on their chemical nature and tissue action.
back:
1. Strong Mineral Acids (e.g., Sulfuric, Nitric)
2. Weak Organic Acids (e.g., Carbolic/Phenol, Oxalic)
3. Strong Alkalis (e.g., Sodium/Potassium hydroxide)
citation: Page 175 (Book Page): [Strong mineral acids are sulfuric acid, nitric acid and hydrochloric acid. Weak organic acids are carbolic acid (phenol), oxalic acid... Important strong alkalis are sodium hydroxide... potassium hydroxide]

category: Classify injuries on the basis of causative weapons
front: Q: How is the 'moving abrasion' graze used to determine weapon movement relative to the body?
back: It indicates the direction of force by showing the heaping or 'piling up' of the epidermis at the far end of the injury.
citation: Page 54 (Book Page): [Moving abrasion indicates direction of abrasive force, showing heaping of piling up of the epidermis on the far end.]

category: Classify injuries on the basis of causative weapons
front: Q: Contrast the wounding characteristics of low-velocity versus high-velocity rifled weapon projectiles.
back:
• Low-velocity: Perforates tissue creating a track proportional to the bullet diameter.
• High-velocity: Dissipates massive energy radially, creating 'temporary cavitation' and shattering bones, causing extensive tissue disintegration.
citation: Page 69 (Book Page): [Low velocity bullet... energy radiates laterally causing damage proportionate to diameter... High velocity bullet... additionally produces a temporary cavitation... disintegrating and disorganization of large areas of the tissue]

category: Classify injuries on the basis of causative weapons
front: Q: How do 'fire-blast' components in a firearm wound differ from a simple mechanical wound?
back: Fire-arms include secondary wounding elements: flame (scorching), hot explosive gases (splitting/blowback), smoke (blackening), and unburned powder (tattooing), which are absent in mechanical wounds.
citation: Page 69 (Book Page): [Fire-blast... contains other elements like flame, hot explosive gases, smoke and some other components of ammunition such as wad, unburned powder and grease]

category: Classify injuries on the basis of causative weapons
front: Q: Classify thermal injuries on the basis of the causative physical state of the heat source.
back:
1. Dry Heat: Flame or heated metallic objects.
2. Moist Heat: Hot liquids (scalds) or pressure steam.
3. Extreme Cold.
citation: Page 62 (Book Page): [Thermal burn is caused by application of heat... whether by heated metallic object, flame, fluids at or near boiling point and pressure steam.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: How is 'Hurt' defined under the Qisas and Diyat Ordinance?
back:
- Causing pain, harm, disease, or infirmity.
- Injury, impairing, disabling, or dismembering any organ.
- Done without causing death.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Hurt is defined as and means causing of pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury or impairing, disabling, dismembering any organ of the body or part thereof withoutt causing death.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Classify the six degrees of Shajjah (hurt on head or face) by severity.
back:
1. Khafifah (No bone exposed)
2. Mudihah (Bone exposed)
3. Hashimah (Fracture without displacement)
4. Munaqqilah (Fracture with displacement)
5. Ammah (Touches brain membrane)
6. Damighah (Ruptures brain membrane)
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Table 4.2... Shajjah-i-Khafifah, Shajjah-i-Mudihah, Shajjah-i-Hashimah, Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah, Shajjah-i-Ammah, Shajjah-i-Damighah.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: What is the primary anatomical distinction between Shajjah and Jurh?
back:
- Shajjah: Injuries specifically located on the head or face.
- Jurh: Injuries on any part of the body other than the head or face.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Table 4.2: Shajjah -> Hurt on the head or face... Jurh -> Hurt on part of the body other than the head and face.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: A victim presents with a head injury where the skull is visible but intact. Diagnosis?
back:
- Shajjah-i-Mudihah.
- Defined as hurt on the head or face where the bone is exposed but not fractured.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Table 4.2: Shajjah-i-Mudihah -> Exposing of bone withoutt its fracture.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Define the three types of financial compensation for hurt: Arsh, Daman, and Diyat.
back:
- Diyat: Compensation specified in law for heirs (usually for death).
- Arsh: Specified compensation for specific types of hurt.
- Daman: Compensation determined by the court for non-Arsh injuries.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Table 4.1: Arsh: Compensation specified in law for causing hurt... Daman: Compensation not liable to Arsh and to be determined by the court... Diyat: Compensation specified in law for causing hurt payable to the heirs.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: What distinguishes Itlaf-i-udw from Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-udw?
back:
- Itlaf-i-udw: Physical dismemberment, amputation, or severing of a limb/organ.
- Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-udw: Destroying the function/capacity of an organ or permanent disfigurement.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Table 4.2: Itlaf-i-udw -> Causing of dismemberment, amputation, severement of any limb or organ... Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-udw -> Destroying of permanently impairing the function or capacity of an organ.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Under Jurh, how is a Jaifah injury defined?
back: - An injury on the trunk (other than head/face) that extends into the body cavity.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Table 4.2: Jaifah -> Hurt extending to the body cavity of the trunk.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Differentiate between Shajjah-i-Ammah and Shajjah-i-Damighah.
back:
- Ammah: The fracture wound merely touches the brain membranes (dura mater).
- Damighah: The injury actually ruptures or punctures the brain membranes.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Table 4.2: Shajjah-i-Ammah -> Fracturing of bone and the wound touching the membranes of brain. Shajjah-i-Damighah -> Fracturing of bone with rupturing of the brain membranes.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Name the first three stages of Ghayr-Jaifah injuries based on tissue depth.
back:
1. Damiyah: Skin rupture with bleeding.
2. Badi'ah: Cutting into flesh without exposing bone.
3. Mutalahimah: Lacerating or deep tearing of flesh.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Table 4.2: Damiyah -> Rupturing of the skin with bleeding. Badi'ah -> Cutting of the flesh withoutt exposing the bone. Mutalahimah -> Lacerating of the flesh.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: What anatomical criteria define Shajjah-i-Hashimah?
back: - A fracture of the skull bone (head or face) without any displacement of the bone fragments.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Table 4.2: Shajjah-i-Hashimah -> Fracturing of bone withoutt displacement.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: How is 'Hurt' defined under the Qisas and Diyat Ordinance 1991?
back: Causing pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury or impairing, disabling, dismembering any organ or part of the body without causing death.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Hurt is defined as and means causing of pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury or impairing, disabling, dismembering any organ of the body or part thereof withoutt causing death.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: What is the functional difference between Itlaf-i-Udw and Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw?
back: Itlaf-i-Udw involves physical dismemberment, amputation, or severing of a limb/organ. Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw involves destroying the function/capacity of an organ or causing permanent disfigurement.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Itlaf-i-Udw: Causing of dismemberment, amputation, severement of any limb or organ of the badly. Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw: Destroying of permanently impairing the function or capacity of an organ of the body or causing permanent disfigurement.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Distinguish between Shajjah-i-Ammah and Shajjah-i-Damighah.
back: Shajjah-i-Ammah involves a fracture where the wound merely touches the brain membranes. Shajjah-i-Damighah involves a fracture that ruptures the brain membranes.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Shajjah-i-Ammah: Fracturing of bone and the wound touching the membranes of brain. Shajjah-i-Damighah: Fracturing of bone with rupturing of the brain membranes.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: A victim presents with a stab wound entering the thoracic cavity; identify this injury class.
back: This is classified as Jaifah, defined as hurt extending into the body cavity of the trunk.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Jaifah: Hurt extending to the body cavity of the trunk.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: What distinguishes Arsh from Daman in terms of compensation determination?
back: Arsh is the compensation specifically fixed and stated in the law. Daman is compensation not specified by law, determined by the court.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Arsh: Compensation specified in law for causing hurt. Daman: Compensation not liable to Arsh and to be determined by the court.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: What are the anatomical boundaries and essential criteria for Shajjah?
back: It must be an injury located specifically on the head or face that does not amount to Itlaf (permanent organ loss).
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Shajjah: Hurt on the head or face which does not amount to Itlaf-i-Udw or itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Classify a non-head injury that results in skin rupture and bleeding.
back: Ghayr-Jaifah Damiyah. It is a sub-type of Jurh (non-head/face injuries) that involves skin rupture with bleeding.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Ghayr-Jaifah: Hurt on part of the body other than the head and face bearing mark of wound. Damiyah: Rupturing of the skin with bleeding.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Contrast the bone involvement in Shajjah-i-Hashimah versus Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah.
back: Hashimah is a bone fracture without displacement. Munaqqilah is a bone fracture with displacement.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Shajjah-i-Hashimah: Fracturing of bone withoutt displacement. Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah: Fracturing of bone with displacement.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Define 'Diyat' as per the legal context of the Act.
back: Diyat is the compensation specified in law for causing hurt, payable by the offender to the heirs of the victim.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Diyat: Compensation specified in law for causing hurt payable to the heirs of the victim, by the offender.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: What is Shajjah-i-Mudihah?
back: An injury to the head or face where the bone is exposed but no fracture has occurred.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Shajjah-i-Mudihah: Exposing of bone withoutt its fracture.

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Under the Qisas and Diyat Act, what is the definition of "Hurt"?
back: Causing pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury, or impairing, disabling, or dismembering any organ or part of the body without causing death.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Hurt is defined as and means causing of pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury or impairing, disabling, dismembering any organ of the body or part thereof without causing death.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Distinguish between Itlaf-i-udw and Itlaf-i-salahiyyat-i-udw.
back:
• Itlaf-i-udw: Dismemberment, amputation, or severing of a limb/organ.
• Itlaf-i-salahiyyat-i-udw: Destroying or permanently impairing the function/capacity of an organ or causing permanent disfigurement.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Itlaf-i-udw: Causing of dismemberment, amputation, severement of any limb or organ of the body. Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-udw: Destroying of permanently impairing the function or capacity of an organ of the body or causing permanent disfigurement.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: What is the primary distinction between Jaifah and Ghayr-jaifah injuries?
back:
• Jaifah: Hurt that extends into a body cavity of the trunk.
• Ghayr-jaifah: Hurt on parts other than the head or face that does not enter a body cavity.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Jaifah: Hurt extending to the body cavity of the trunk. Ghayr-jaifah: Hurt on part of the body other than the head and face... not amounting to Jaifah.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: An assailant strikes a victim's forehead, exposing the bone without fracturing it. Classify this head injury.
back: Shajjah-i-mudihah.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-mudihah: Exposing of bone without its fracture.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: List the six sub-types of Shajjah (head/face injuries) in order of severity.
back:
1. Khafifah (no bone exposed)
2. Mudihah (exposed bone)
3. Hashimah (fracture)
4. Munaqqilah (displaced fracture)
5. Ammah (touches brain membrane)
6. Damighah (ruptures brain membrane).
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Hurt on the head or face... Shajjah-i-khafifah... Shajjah-i-mudihah... Shajjah-i-hashimah... Shajjah-i-munaqqilah... Shajjah-i-ammah... Shajjah-i-damighah.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: What anatomical boundary defines the category of "Shajjah"?
back: Hurt located specifically on the head or face which does not amount to Itlaf-i-udw or Itlaf-i-salahiyyat-i-udw.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Shajjah: Hurt on the head or face which does not amount to itlaf-i-Udw or itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Define the legal difference between Arsh and Daman compensation.
back:
• Arsh: Fixed compensation specified by law for causing specific hurts.
• Daman: Compensation determined by the court for injuries not liable to Arsh.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Arsh: Compensation specified in law for causing hurt... Daman: Compensation not liable to Arsh and to be determined by the court.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: A victim sustains a 3cm deep stab to the chest versus the thigh. Differentiate the classification.
back:
• Chest wound: Jaifah (extends to trunk cavity).
• Thigh wound: Ghayr-jaifah (no cavity involvement).
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Jaifah: Hurt extending to the body cavity of the trunk. Ghayr-jaifah: Hurt on part of the body other than the head and face... not amounting to Jaifah.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Contrast brain membrane involvement in Shajjah-i-ammah vs. Shajjah-i-damighah.
back:
• Ammah: Fracture where the wound merely touches the brain membranes (meninges).
• Damighah: Fracture where the brain membranes are actually ruptured.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-ammah: Fracturing of bone and the wound touching the membranes of brain. Shajjah-i-damighah: Fracturing of bone with rupturing of the brain membranes.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: What is the defining feature of Ghayr-jaifah "Damiyah"?
back: A hurt on the body (excluding head/face) involving the rupturing of the skin with bleeding.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Ghayr-jaifah... Damiyah: Rupturing of the skin with bleeding.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act

back:

• Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw: Destroying/impairing function/capacity or causing permanent disfigurement.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Itlaf-i-Udw: Causing of dismemberment, amputation, severement of any limb or organ... Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw: Destroying of permanently impairing the function or capacity of an organ... or causing permanent disfigurement.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: What is the anatomical distinction between Shajjah and Jurh?
back:
• Shajjah: Injuries specifically on the head or face.
• Jurh: Injuries on any part of the body other than head or face.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Shajjah: Hurt on the head or face... Jurh: Hurt on part of the body other than the head and face.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Classify a head injury where the bone is exposed but not fractured.
back: Shajjah Mudihah.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Shajjah Mudihah: Exposing of bone withoutt its fracture.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Differentiate between the legal compensations Arsh and Daman.
back:
• Arsh: Compensation specified in the law for causing specific hurts.
• Daman: Compensation determined by the court (not specified by law).
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Arsh: Compensation specified in law... Daman: Compensation not liable to Arsh and to be determined by the court.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: What is the defining feature of a Jaifah injury?
back: A Jurh (body injury) that extends into the body cavity of the trunk (e.g., abdomen or chest).
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Jaifah: Hurt extending to the body cavity of the trunk.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Contrast Shajjah Ammah and Shajjah Damighah regarding brain involvement.
back:
• Ammah: Fracture touching the brain membranes.
• Damighah: Fracture involving actual rupturing of brain membranes.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Shajjah Ammah: Fracturing of bone and the wound touching the membranes of brain. Shajjah Damighah: Fracturing of bone with rupturing of the brain membranes.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: A victim suffers a leg injury that exposes the bone. Provide the exact legal sub-classification.
back: Jurh Ghayr-Jaifah Mudihah.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Hurt on part of the body other than the head and face... Ghayr-Jaifah Mudihah: the fas exposing the bone. (Shosp weapon)]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Define Jurh Ghayr-Jaifah Damiyah.
back: A hurt on parts other than head/face involving rupturing of the skin with bleeding.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Ghayr-Jaifah Damiyah: Rupturing of the skin with bleeding.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: What is the mildest form of Shajjah and its key feature?
back: Shajjah Khafifah; hurt on the head or face without exposing the bone.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Shajjah Khafifah: Hurt withoutt exposing of bone.]

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Define 'Hurt' as per the Qisas and Diyat Ordinance.
back: Causing pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury, or impairing/disabling/dismembering any organ without causing death.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Hurt is defined as and means causing of pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury or impairing, disabling, dismembering any organ of the body or part thereof withoutt causing death.

back:

category: Classify injuries as per Qisas and Diyyat Act
front: Q: Classify a head injury involving a skull fracture that ruptures the brain membranes.
back: Shajjah-i-damighah.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Shajjah-i-damighah: Fracturing of bone with rupturing of the brain membranes.
