back: Red-granulation tissue typically forms in the wound bed between five to six days post-injury.
citation: Page 60 (Book Page): [followed by formation of red-granulation tissue in the bed of the wound in about five to six days]

category: Illustrate stages of healing of fractures of bones
front: Q: What is the total healing time to reach a fresh scar in a slightly septic injury?
back: Healing in slightly septic cases is typically completed in twelve to sixteen days.
citation: Page 60 (Book Page): [skin grows over it and healing gets completed in twelve to sixteen days. Fresh scar in such a wound is more prominent and slightly raised over the surface of the skin]

category: Illustrate stages of healing of fractures of bones
front: Q: When does thrombo-phlebitis typically develop as a complication of a lower limb fracture?
back: Thrombo-phlebitis, which increases blood viscosity and platelet adhesiveness, develops in about two weeks following the injury.
citation: Page 87 (Book Page): [thrombo-phlebitis, which develops in about two weeks following an injury.]

category: Illustrate stages of healing of fractures of bones
front: Q: Why is forensic age estimation impossible in grossly septic fractures or wounds?
back: Grossly septic wounds remain open indefinitely, preventing any reliable estimation of the age of the injury.
citation: Page 60 (Book Page): [Grossly septic wound remains open indefinitely and no estimation of age is possible]

category: Interpret and document the nature of the fracture in the injury certificate as per Qisas and Diyat act
front: Q: Define Shajjah according to the Qisas and Diyat Ordinance.
back: Hurt inflicted specifically on the head or face which does not amount to Itlaf-i-Udw (dismemberment) or Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw (loss of function).
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Shajjah: Hurt on the head or face which does not amount to Itlaf-i-Udw or itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw.]

category: Interpret and document the nature of the fracture in the injury certificate as per Qisas and Diyat act
front: Q: How is a fracture of the skull or face without displacement documented?
back: Documented as Shajjah-i-Hashimah. It involves fracturing the bone without displacing it.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Hashimah: Fracturing of bone without displacement.]

category: Interpret and document the nature of the fracture in the injury certificate as per Qisas and Diyat act
front: Q: Contrast Shajjah-i-Hashimah and Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah in an injury certificate.
back:
• Shajjah-i-Hashimah: Fracture without displacement.
• Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah: Fracture with displacement of the bone.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Hashimah: Fracturing of bone without displacement. Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah: Fracturing of bone with displacement.]

category: Interpret and document the nature of the fracture in the injury certificate as per Qisas and Diyat act
front: Q: A victim presents with a facial fracture exposing the brain membranes. Classify this hurt.
back: Shajjah-i-Ammah. It involves fracturing the head or face bone where the wound touches the membranes of the brain.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Ammah: Fracturing of bone and the wound touching the membranes of brain.]

category: Interpret and document the nature of the fracture in the injury certificate as per Qisas and Diyat act
front: Q: Differentiate Arsh from Daman in the documentation of fractures.
back:
• Arsh: Compensation specified in law for causing hurt.
• Daman: Compensation not liable to Arsh, determined by the court and payable by the offender to the victim.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Arsh: Compensation specified in law for causing hurt... Daman: Compensation not liable to Arsh and to be determined by the court for causing hurt.]

category: Interpret and document the nature of the fracture in the injury certificate as per Qisas and Diyat act
front: Q: What is the legal classification for exposing a head bone without fracturing it?
back: Shajjah-i-Mudihah. This classification applies when the bone is exposed but remains intact (no fracture).
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Mudihah: Exposing of bone without its fracture.]

category: Interpret and document the nature of the fracture in the injury certificate as per Qisas and Diyat act
front: Q: How are limb fractures classified under the Ghayr-Jaifah category?
back:
• Ghayr-Jaifah Hashimah: Fracture of bone without displacement.
• Ghayr-Jaifah Munaqqilah: Fracture of bone with displacement.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Ghayr-Jaifah Hashimah: Fracturing of bone. Ghayr-Jaifah Munaqqilah: Fracturing of bone with displacement.]

category: Interpret and document the nature of the fracture in the injury certificate as per Qisas and Diyat act
front: Q: A victim has a compound leg fracture with bone displacement. Document this under Qisas and Diyat.
back: Ghayr-Jaifah Munaqqilah. It applies to hurts on parts other than the head/face involving a displaced fracture.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Ghayr-Jaifah Munaqqilah: Fracturing of bone with displacement.]

category: Interpret and document the nature of the fracture in the injury certificate as per Qisas and Diyat act
front: Q: Define Shajjah-i-Damighah in forensic documentation.
back: Fracturing of the skull or face bone with actual rupturing of the brain membranes (dura mater).
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Damighah: Fracturing of bone with rupturing of the brain membranes.]

category: Interpret and document the nature of the fracture in the injury certificate as per Qisas and Diyat act
front: Q: Define Jurh and its relationship to Jaifah.
back:
• Jurh: Hurt on any part of the body other than head/face bearing a wound mark.
• Jaifah: A Jurh extending into the body cavity of the trunk.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Jurh: Hurt on part of the body other than the head and face... Jaifah: Hurt extending to the body cavity of the trunk.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: How are bone fractures mechanically classified based on force application?
back:
- Direct application: Fracture occurs at the strike site.
- Indirect application: Fracture occurs at a remote weaker point via leverage or twisting.
citation: Page 60 (Book Page): [Bone fracture takes place either by direct mechanical application of force or impact or indirect application of force. Long and skull bones are mainly affected]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Contrast long bone fractures in children versus adults regarding elasticity.
back:
- Children: More elastic, resulting in 'Greenstick' fractures (damage to one side).
- Adults: Brittle, breaking at the point of impact or acting as a lever to distant points.
citation: Page 60 (Book Page): [Long bones of children are comparatively more elastic and show less damage to only one side of bone close to application of force resulting in greenstick — fracture.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Describe Rowbotham's local deformation sequence at a skull impact site.
back:
- Formation of a shallow cone.
- Apex stretches and fractures the inner-table first.
- Periphery compresses and fractures the outer-table.
- Results in a comminuted depressed fracture.
citation: Page 61 (Book Page): [Sequence of events at the site of impact is formation of a shallow cone. Apex of cone stretches the inner-table and compresses the outer table ... a fracture confined to the inner-table at the apex of cone results.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: In general skull deformation (compression), where do fractures typically occur?
back:
- Fractures occur at parts of the skull distant from the force site.
- Usually fissured fractures in the vertical and longitudinal planes as the sphere bulges.
citation: Page 61 (Book Page): [Skull when compressed laterally, it elongates in its vertical and longitudinal plane, producing fractures in these planes. These fractures are usually fissured ones occurring at parts of skull distant from actual site of application of force.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: What is the medico-legal significance of a fractured inner-table of the skull?
back:
- Leads to adhesions between the dura-mater and brain substance.
- May precipitate traumatic epilepsy as a long-term complication.
citation: Page 61 (Book Page): [Complication of the fracture of the inner-table leads to the development of adhesions betweenn dura-matter and brain substance and may precipitate traumatic epilepsy.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: List Gustafson’s six criteria for dental age estimation in adults.
back:
1. Attrition
2. Periodontosis
3. Secondary dentine
4. Cementum deposit
5. Root resorption
6. Translucency of root (most reliable).
citation: Page 47 (Book Page): [He observed that teeth damage and repair changes are of Six types... Attrition, Periodontosis, Secondary dentine, Cementum deposit around root, root resorption, translucency of the root.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: What forensic importance does the arrangement of teeth hold in identification?
back:
- Tooth arrangement is individual-specific and visible during life.
- Bite imprints on victims provide indisputable evidence of an assailant's identity.
citation: Page 48 (Book Page): [arrangement of tooth is individual’s specific... teeth bite imprints are also specific when caused on human skin and food stuff... providing indisputable evidence of assailant’s persons identity after matching with control]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Provide two examples of civil medical negligence involving bones or teeth.
back:
1. Extraction of a healthy tooth instead of a diseased one.
2. Failure to X-ray a fractured bone during treatment.
citation: Page 21 (Book Page): [Civil negligence results from lack of carefulness... common examples are extraction of a healthy tooth instead of diseased one; failure to X-ray a fractured bone]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: In industrial accidents, what fatal complication arises from limb crushing and fractures?
back:
- Fat embolism occurs following crushing of bones and adipose tissue.
- Can lead to systemic collapse and death.
citation: Page 84 (Book Page): [secondary fat embolism... may occurs following trauma to the body, more so in crushing injury of the limbs especially when associated with fractured soft tissues like muscles and adipose tissue.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Why are teeth and bones preferred in identifying decomposed remains?
back:
- Dentine and enamel are the most durable and hardest body tissues.
- They withstand decomposition and fire indefinitely.
citation: Page 45 (Book Page): [Dentine is... the most durable of all body tissues. It is covered by crown of... enamel which is the hardest of all tissues... teeth supporting bony tissues are characterized to an individual, indestructible in fire and also withstand decomposition]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: What constitutes civil negligence in the medical management of bone fractures?
back:
* Failure to X-ray a fractured bone
* Results in liability for compensation in terms of money
* Recoverable damages include physical injury and loss of earning capacity.
citation: Page 24 (Book Page): [Civil negligence results from lack of carefulness during medical treatment and common examples are... failure to X-ray a fractured bone]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Distinguish Shajjah-i-Hashimah from Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah in legal classification.
back:
* Shajjah-i-Hashimah: Fracturing of bone without displacement.
* Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah: Fracturing of bone with displacement.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Hashimah: Fracturing of bone withoutt displacement. Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah: Fracturing of bone with displacement.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Define Shajjah-i-Ammah versus Shajjah-i-Damighah regarding brain involvement.
back:
* Shajjah-i-Ammah: Fracture touching the membranes of the brain.
* Shajjah-i-Damighah: Fracture with rupturing of the brain membranes.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Ammah: Fracturing of bone and the wound touching the membranes of brain. Shajjah-i-Damighah: Fracturing of bone with rupturing of the brain membranes.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: What specific anatomical features of the mandible assist in age determination?
back:
* Shape of the ramus and processes
* Status of dentition and alveolar ridge
* Position of the mental foramen
* Presence of muscular attachment markings.
citation: Page 45 (Book Page): [Age changes in mandible should be considered in relationship to Shape of the jaw as a whole especially at various parts (ramus, condyloid and coronoid processes), dentition, alveolar ridge, muscular attachment marking and position of the mental foramen.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Why are tooth bite marks forensically significant in physical assaults?
back:
* Act as individual-specific traits
* Provide indisputable evidence of assailant's identity
* Requires matching with suspected controls.
citation: Page 48 (Book Page): [Such bite imprint can act as good means that can be utterly relied upon for personal identity of aggressor in cases of physical/sexual assault. Though rare, yet is an important finding providing indisputable evidence of assailant’s personal identity after matching with control]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
coreConcept: Threshold of Bone Injury in Law
front: Q: Distinguish Shajjah-i-Mudiha from the fracture-based Shajjah categories.
back:
* Shajjah-i-Mudiha: Exposing the bone WITHOUT fracture.
* It is the threshold category before bone breakage is legally recognized.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Mudiha: Exposing of bone withoutt its fracture.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Explain the mechanism and legal significance of a 'Greenstick' fracture.
back:
* Found in children due to high bone elasticity
* Results in damage to only one side of the bone
* Common in Battered Baby Syndrome via indirect force.
citation: Page 60 (Book Page): [Long bones of children are comparatively more elastic and show less damage to only one side of bone close to application of force resulting in green stick fracture... as generally seen in battered baby syndrome.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: What is the medico-legal importance of an inner-table skull fracture?
back:
* May lead to adhesions between dura-mater and brain substance
* Can precipitate traumatic epilepsy.
citation: Page 61 (Book Page): [Complication of the fracture of the inner-table leads to the development of adhesions betweenn dura-matter and brain substance and may precipitate traumatic epilepsy.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Contrast the effects of slight versus great force on bone based on elasticity.
back:
* Slight Force: Causes local indentation and recoils back (within limit of elasticity).
* Great Force: Causes fracture at the point of maximum convexity (beyond limit of elasticity).
citation: Page 60 (Book Page): [Slight force within the limit of bone elasticity will cause a local indentation at site of impact withoutt breaking bone and then recoil back... Great force beyond the limit of bone elasticity causes fracture at point of maximum convexity]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: What is the primary role of forensic radiology in medico-legal bone examination?
back:
* To visualize hidden fractures or joint dislocations
* To locate and record projectiles (e.g., bullets/shot-charge)
* Provides permanent evidence for court use.
citation: Page 108 (Book Page): [Forensic radiology is specialized investigation to help seek out that what is hidden (bone fracture/ joint dislocation and firearm short-charge) Providing Permanent record acceptable to courts]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Define Shajjah-i-Hashimah according to the Pakistan Penal Code (Qisas and Diyat Ordinance).
back:
* Fracturing a bone of the head or face.
* Specifically occurs without displacement of the bone fragments.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Hashimah: Fracturing of bone without displacement.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Explain the mechanical basis for greenstick fractures occurring in pediatric victims.
back:
* Pediatric long bones are more elastic than adult bones.
* Force causes damage to only one side of the bone, avoiding complete breakage.
citation: Page 60 (Book Page): [Long bones of children are comparatively more elastic and show less damage to only one side of bone resulting in green stick — fracture.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Differentiate between Shajjah-i-Ammah and Shajjah-i-Damighah regarding brain involvement.
back:
* Ammah: The fracture and wound touch the brain membranes (dura mater).
* Damighah: The fracture causes the actual rupturing of the brain membranes.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Ammah: Fracturing of bone and the wound touching the brain membranes. Shajjah-i-Damighah: Fracturing of bone with rupturing of the brain membranes.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: A victim sustains a basal skull fracture from a mandibular strike. Identify this mechanism.
back:
* Indirect application of force.
* Force is transmitted from the mandible to the weakest portion, the cribriform plate of ethmoid.
citation: Page 61 (Book Page): [Occasionally force from the face like a blow on the mandible, may be transmitted to the base of the skull, fracturing the weakest portion namely cribriform plate of ethmoid.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: What is the primary technical requirement for certifying a bone fracture as forensic evidence?
back:
* Radiography (X-ray).
* It identifies the site/type of fracture and provides a permanent record for the court.
citation: Page 110 (Book Page): [Forensic investigations are those... X-ray of bone or joint to know site and type of fracture... They provide permanent record and are acceptable as evidence to Courts.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Define Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah in terms of the state of the fractured bone.
back:
* Fracture of a bone of the head or face.
* The defining feature is the presence of bone displacement.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah: Fracturing of bone with displacement.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: How is the criminal loss of a tooth classified under Qisas and Diyat Ordinance?
back:
* Itlaf-i-Udw.
* This involves dismemberment, amputation, or severing of an organ or limb of the body.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Itlaf-i-Udw: Causing of dismemberment, amputation, severement of any limb or organ of the badly [sic]]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Contrast Rowhbotham’s local deformation versus general deformation in skull fractures.
back:
* Local: Crushing of the outer table into the diploe at the site of impact.
* General: Compression in one plane causing outward bulging/fracture in another plane.
citation: Page 61 (Book Page): [Rowhbotham divides mechanism of fracturing of skull into; local deformation at the site and general deformation of the whole skull.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: What physiological outcome occurs when a force applied to bone is within its elastic limit?
back:
* Local indentation at the site of impact.
* The bone recoils to its original shape without sustaining a fracture.
citation: Page 60 (Book Page): [Slight force within the limit of bone elasticity will cause a local indentation at site of impact withoutt breaking bone and then recoil back to its original shape.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Identify two biological properties of teeth that make them vital for postmortem identity.
back:
* Indestructibility: They are the hardest and most durable body tissues.
* Decomposition resistance: They remain recognizable after soft tissues putrefy.
citation: Page 48 (Book Page): [teeth... are individual specific, indestructible in life and also withstand decomposition.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the direction of ligature marks in hanging versus strangulation.
back: Hanging: Oblique, directed upward toward the knot. Strangulation: Horizontal, directed transversely across the neck.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Hanging: Oblique... Strangulation: Horizontal]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: How does the continuity of the ligature mark differ in hanging versus strangulation?
back: Hanging: In-continuous/incomplete (absent at the knot site). Strangulation: Continuous/complete (runs all around the neck).
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Hanging: Incomplete... Strangulation: Complete]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the level of the neck where marks typically occur in these two conditions.
back: Hanging: High up, usually above the thyroid cartilage. Strangulation: Mid-neck, usually over or below the thyroid cartilage.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Hanging: High up in the neck... Strangulation: Middle of neck]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: A body presents with a horizontal ligature mark of uniform depth. Diagnosis?
back: Ligature Strangulation. In hanging, depth is non-uniform, being deepest opposite the knot and shallowest near it.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Strangulation: Horizontal... Uniform depth]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the knot position typically found in hanging versus homicidal strangulation.
back: Hanging: Usually on the back of the neck (occipital). Strangulation: Typically firmly tied in front.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Hanging: on back of neck... Strangulation: In front of neck]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: What is the frequency of laryngeal fractures in hanging compared to strangulation?
back: Hanging: Rare (approx. 3-5%). Strangulation: Common; hyoid bone and thyroid cartilage are frequently fractured.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Hanging: Fracture of hyoid bone... rare finding occurring only in about 3-5% cases... Strangulation: Hyoid bone usually... fractured.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the intensity of cyanosis and petechial hemorrhages between these two modes of death.
back: Strangulation: Intense cyanosis and profuse petechiae. Hanging: Scanty petechiae and mild or absent cyanosis.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Hanging: Cyanosis: Mild or absent... Strangulation: Intense... Petechaeal: Scanty... Intense]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: How do the number of ligature loops typically differ between hanging and strangulation?
back: Hanging: Usually a single turn. Strangulation: Often involves multiple turns around the neck.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Hanging: Single turn... Strangulation: More turns]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Describe the mechanism of constricting force applied in hanging versus strangulation.
back: Hanging: Indirect force applied through the weight of the body. Strangulation: Direct force applied to the ligature by an agent.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page)-153: [Hanging: constricting force being applied indirectly through weight of the body... Strangulation: constricting force being applied directly to ligature.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: What is a distinguishing mark on the neck found in strangulation but absent in hanging?
back: Vertical nail marks/scratches are often present in strangulation (indicating a struggle) but are absent in hanging.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Hanging: Nail marks: Absent... Strangulation: Present (parallel vertical above ligature mark)]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the direction of the neck ligature mark in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: Oblique (upward towards the knot).
• Strangulation: Horizontal/Transverse (all around the neck).
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [Direction of the mark is oblique going upward towards the knot... Directed transversely across it (Strangulation).]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the continuity of the neck mark in hanging versus ligature strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: In-continuous; absent at the knot position.
• Strangulation: Continuous; encircles the neck completely.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page)/153: [characteristic is that it is in-continuous and absent at the place against knot... It is all around the neck (Strangulation).]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Compare the typical level of the ligature mark on the neck for both conditions.
back:
• Hanging: High up, usually above the thyroid cartilage.
• Strangulation: Lower down, situated at the level of or below the larynx.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Site: High up in the neck (Hanging) - Middle of neck (Strangulation).]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: A body is found with a horizontal, uniform-depth mark below the larynx. Diagnosis?
back:
• Diagnosis: Ligature Strangulation.
• Rationale: Hanging marks are oblique, non-uniform in depth, and typically located above the thyroid cartilage.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Direction: Oblique (Hanging) - Horizontal (Strangulation). Depth of the groove: Decreases towards knot - Uniform.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Compare the intensity of cyanosis and facial congestion in hanging vs strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: Nil or very mild.
• Strangulation: Intense cyanosis and marked facial congestion due to venous return obstruction.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Cyanosis: Nil or absent (Hanging) - Intense (Strangulation). Facial congestion: May be present - Marked.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the prevalence of Tardieu’s spots (petechiae) in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: Scanty or absent petechiae.
• Strangulation: Numerous and prominent petechial hemorrhages in the face and viscera.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Petechaeal hemorrhage: Scanty (Hanging) - Numerous (Strangulation).]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Describe the depth of the ligature groove in a typical hanging victim.
back: Non-uniform depth; it is deepest opposite the knot and becomes shallower as it approaches the knot.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [depth of the groove is not uniform being deepest at a point opposite to the knot and gradually becoming shallower towards it.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Which specific internal fracture is highly diagnostic but rare in hanging cases?
back:
• Fracture of the hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage.
• Frequency: Occurs in only 3-5% of hanging cases.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Fracture of hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage is a rare finding occurring only in about 3-5% cases (Hanging).]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: What is the mechanism of immediate death in judicial or sudden-drop hanging?
back:
• Mechanism: Vagal inhibition or reflex cardiac arrest.
• Cause: Stimulation of carotid sinus/vagus nerve or upper cervical spinal cord separation.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [Death by vagal inhibition resultant from pressure over carotid sinus or vagus nerve and due to sudden drop... is immediate.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the role of body weight in hanging versus ligature strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: Force is indirect via body weight.
• Strangulation: Force is applied directly to the ligature by an external agent.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page)/153: [Hanging: constricting force being applied indirectly through weight of the body. Strangulation: constricting force being applied directly to ligature.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: What is the primary skeletal index for age attainment at 25 years?
back: The final union of the epiphysis with the diaphysis in most long bones.
citation: Page 40 (Book Page): [union of epiphysis with diaphysis is the index unto the attainment of twenty fifth year of age]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Describe the pathological mechanism of fat embolism following a long bone fracture.
back: Crushing of bone and adipose tissue releases fat droplets into circulation, causing fatal pulmonary or systemic obstruction.
citation: Page 84 (Book Page): [Fat embolism follows trauma to the body, more so in crushing of the limbs especially when associated with fractured long bones and soft tissues like muscles and adipose tissue]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Contrast bone fracture patterns in children versus adults regarding medico-legal significance.
back: Children exhibit elastic greenstick fractures (partial breaks); adults exhibit brittle fractures or comminution (complete shattering) under similar force.
citation: Page 60 (Book Page): [Long bones of children are comparatively more elastic and show less damage to only one side of bone... resulting in green stick fracture.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: A victim develops fatal meningitis after a head injury. Which fracture likely occurred?
back: A fracture of the anterior fossa of the skull, which provides a route for infection.
citation: Page 84 (Book Page): [not obvious cases are the development of meningitis and pneumonia following fracture of anterior fossa of the skull]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Which dental diagnostic step is most reliable for identifying the age of a mature adult?
back: The measurement of root translucency (one of the six Gustafson criteria).
citation: Page 47 (Book Page): [translucency of root alone is the most reliable of all of Gustafson’s criteria for measurement of age.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: List the three primary forensic objectives of examining bone and tooth fractures.
back:
1. Identification (age/sex/race). 
2. Determining cause and manner of death. 
3. Assessing injury gravity for compensation.
citation: Page 106 (Book Page): [Forensic examinations... of physical/sexual assault... objectives... establishment of personal identity, determination of cause and manner of death]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: How are teeth bite marks used to establish a suspect's personal identification?
back: Individual-specific tooth arrangements and bite imprints on skin or food are matched against suspect controls.
citation: Page 48 (Book Page): [arrangement of tooth is individual’s specific... such bite imprint can act as good means that can be utterly relied upon for personal identity of aggressor]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: A deceased exhibits a fractured superior horn of the thyroid cartilage. Interpret this finding.
back: It is a characteristic indicator of manual strangulation (throttling) due to localized neck compression.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Decomposition may present difficulties... and diagnosis of throttling will mainly depend upon presence of fracture of thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Explain the physiological loop leading to renal failure in massive crushing bone trauma.
back: Crushing release of acid metabolites and myoglobin combined with renal ischemia causes tubular necrosis and failure.
citation: Page 84 (Book Page): [Crush syndrome... due to attempt on the part of kidney to excrete acid metabolites from damaged muscles... current view... due to renal ischemia]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Which specific bone provides 98% accuracy in identifying the sex of a victim?
back: The pelvis (including the sacrum).
citation: Page 49 (Book Page): [Bones have a high percentage of accuracy for the determination of sex. Table 5.7: Pelvis 98%]

category: Explain medico legal importance of bruises
front: Q: How does a bruise’s shape contribute to its medico-legal importance regarding the weapon used?
back: A bruise typically acquires the specific shape of the striking blunt weapon, providing physical evidence to identify the causative object.
citation: Page 55 (Book Page): [A bruise generally acquires the shape of striking weapon.]

category: Explain medico legal importance of bruises
front: Q: What is the underlying mechanism responsible for the swelling and redness in a fresh bruise?
back: A blunt strike causes sudden tissue indentation and recoil, resulting in broken capillaries and blood extravasation into the surrounding interstitial tissue.
citation: Page 55 (Book Page): [It results from sudden tissue indentation followed by recoil. Area struck becomes swollen, red and painful... Extravasations of blood from the broken vessels spread into the surrounding tissue.]

category: Explain medico legal importance of bruises
front: Q: Distinguish a bruise from post-mortem pseudo-bruising based on the state of the blood vessels.
back:
• Bruise: Vessels are ruptured with blood in interstitial spaces.
• Pseudo-bruising: Blood is stagnant within the vessels; no extravasation occurs.
citation: Page 57 (Book Page): [Bruise (Anti-mortem): Blood vessels are broken and blood is present in surrounding inter-statius tissue... Pseudo-bruising (Post-mortem): Blood is contained within the vessels.]

category: Explain medico legal importance of bruises
front: Q: Why is a second inspection recommended 24 hours after a victim's initial forehead trauma?
back: Gravity causes blood to shift along tissue lines of least resistance, potentially manifesting as a 'black eye' away from the original injury site.
citation: Page 56 (Book Page): [Gravity shifting of bruise occurs from its initial site along tissue line of least resistance... It is advisable and valuable to re-examine victim after about twenty-four hours after the first inspection.]

category: Explain medico legal importance of bruises
front: Q: What biochemical change occurs in a bruise at the 48-hour mark to alter its color?
back: The bruise darkens to purple as the oxygen within the extravasated capillary blood is removed.
citation: Page 56 (Book Page): [Capillary blood is dark red in color and a recent bruise appears purple in color; it darkens in two days because oxygen in the blood is removed.]

category: Explain medico legal importance of bruises
front: Q: List the diagnostic criteria for a bruise to be considered 'ante-mortem' during forensic certification.
back: A true bruise must exhibit vital reactions such as local swelling, redness, and inflammatory changes.
citation: Page 57 (Book Page): [Area showing pseudo-bruising lacks vital reaction. Importance in distinction lies in the fact that bruising is an ante-mortem phenomenon... showing vital reaction (swelling and inflammation).]

category: Explain medico legal importance of bruises
front: Q: What is the significance of finding bruises on internal organs like the liver or kidney during autopsy?
back: It indicates violence occurred during life (ante-mortem) and helps distinguish trauma from localized post-mortem lividity (hypostasis).
citation: Page 56 (Book Page): [But bruising of internal organs like liver and kidney also occurs... Importance in distinction lies in the fact that bruising is an ante-mortem phenomenon indicating violence before death.]

category: Explain medico legal importance of bruises
front: Q: Why do systemic diseases like liver cirrhosis create a misleading medico-legal impression of trauma severity?
back: Coagulation defects cause disproportionately excessive bleeding, making a minor impact appear as a severe injury.
citation: Page 56 (Book Page): [State of health (coagulation defect, disease of blood vessel and liver cause more bleeding giving false impression about severity)]

category: Explain medico legal importance of bruises
front: Q: Describe the physiological loop causing the rapid color change observed in 'police battering' cases.
back: Repeated strikes interfere with oxygenation and enzyme action, causing blood to darken to deep blue/black within hours instead of days.
citation: Page 57 (Book Page): [Repeated strikes... interferes with oxygenation/enzyme action and accelerates color change from first two days to few hours causing rapid darkening of effused blood to deep blue/black color.]

category: Explain medico legal importance of bruises
front: Q: In which specific anatomical layer is a bruise's extravasated blood primarily located?
back: The blood pools in the interstitial tissue below the epidermis.
citation: Page 57 (Book Page): [Lies in the inter-statius tissue below epidermis or even deeper to it, as epidermis is without blood vessels.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: How are bone fractures classified based on the application of mechanical force?
back:
1. Direct: At the point of impact.
2. Indirect: Remote from the impact site (e.g., clavicle fracture from a fall on the palm).
citation: Page 53 (Book Page): Wounding when Cauved mechanionlly in called mechanical injuries... There are two manners of execution of infliction of weapon; direct and indirect. Indirect causes injury at a place away from impact site like fracture of clavicle produced by fall on palm.

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Describe the forensic characteristic and mechanism of a 'green stick' fracture.
back:
1. Mechanism: Force exceeding elasticity in children's bones.
2. Feature: Damage is limited to only one side of the bone close to the force application.
citation: Page 60 (Book Page): Long bones of children are comparatively more elastic and show less damage to only one side of bone close to application of force resulting in green stick — fracture.

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Differentiate between local and general deformation mechanisms in skull fractures.
back:
1. Local: Crushing of the outer table or bending at the impact site (e.g., depressed fracture).
2. General: Compression in one plane causes bulging and fissured fractures in another plane.
citation: Page 61 (Book Page): Rowhbotham divides mechanigm of fracturing of skull into; local deformation at the site and general deformation of the whole skull... Local deformation at the site occurs, if the force applied is sufficient to cause crushing... General deformation of whole skull occurs due to COND Tress] of the skull.

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: What specific bone injury can lead to traumatic epilepsy as a late complication?
back: Fracture of the inner-table of the skull, which causes adhesions between the dura-mater and brain substance.
citation: Page 61 (Book Page): Complication of the fracture of the inner-table leads to the development of adhesions betweenn dura-matter and brain substance and may precipitate traumatic epilepsy.

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: List the six criteria used in Gustafson’s method for adult age estimation from teeth.
back:
1. Attrition
2. Periodontosis
3. Secondary dentine
4. Cementum deposition
5. Root resorption
6. Transparency of the root.
citation: Page 47 (Book Page): Table 5.6: Gustafson's criteria... Alteration in level of gingival attachment (P)... Transtucency of the root (T)... Cementum deposit around root (C)... Attrition (A)... Secondary dentine (S)... root resorption (R).

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Why are teeth considered superior for personal identification in mass disasters?
back:
1. Enamel is the hardest tissue in the body.
2. Dentine is the most durable tissue.
3. They withstand decomposition and high heat.
citation: Page 45 (Book Page): Dentine is highly mineralized material... the most durable of all body tissues. It is covered by... enamel which is the hardest of all tissues... teeth supporting bony tissues are Charautenyry to an individual, indestrucble io fie and also withstand decompositions.

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Under the Qisas and Diyat Ordinance, define the hurt 'Shajjah-i-Hashimah'.
back: It is defined as fracturing a bone of the head or face without causing displacement.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Table 4.2: Shajjah-i-Hashimah: Fracturing of bone withoutt displacement.

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Under Shajjah, what distinguishes 'Munaqqilah' from 'Ammah' fractures?
back:
1. Munaqqilah: Fracture of head/face bone with displacement.
2. Ammah: Fracture where the wound touches the membranes of the brain.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Table 4.2: Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah: Fracturing of bone with displacement. Shajjah-i-Ammah: Fracturing of bone and the wound touching the eas of brain.

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Provide two specific examples of civil medical negligence involving bones or teeth.
back:
1. Extraction of a healthy tooth instead of a diseased one.
2. Failure to X-ray a suspected fractured bone.
citation: Page 21 (Book Page): Civil negligence results from lack of carefulness during medical treatment and common examples are extraction of a healthy tooth instead of diseased one: failure to X-ray a fractured bone.

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: How is the direction of fire determined in a rifled firearm wound to the skull?
back: The entry hole is typically clean, while the exit hole shows internal/external 'beveling' of the skull margins.
citation: Page 73 (Book Page): Only skull shows characteristic entry and exit piffled ballet holes, which indicate direction. of trajectory. Entry hole is a simple hole, whereas exit shows beveled Margins.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Compare the typical direction of ligature marks observed in hanging versus strangulation cases.
back:
- Hanging: Oblique, directed upward toward the site of the knot.
- Strangulation: Transverse (horizontal), completely encircling the neck.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Direction - Hanging: Oblique. Strangulation: Horizontal.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: What are the three primary physiological mechanisms leading to death in mechanical neck constriction?
back:
- Cerebral anoxia (venous/arterial compression).
- Asphyxia (tongue/larynx obstructing airway).
- Reflex cardiac arrest (carotid sinus/vagus nerve stimulation).
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [Mechanism of death in hanging includes cerebral anoxia, reflex cardiac arrest and asphyxia by lifting of glottis and tongue into pharynx and obstructing airway.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: How does the continuity of the ligature mark distinguish hanging from strangulation?
back:
- Hanging: In-continuous (incomplete); the mark is absent at the location of the knot.
- Strangulation: Continuous (complete); the mark encircles the entire neck circumference.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [characteristic is that it is in-continuous and absent at the place against knot.] Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Extent - Hanging: Incomplete. Strangulation: Complete.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: A corpse exhibits a horizontal neck groove. Which finding confirms the injury occurred ante-mortem?
back: - The presence of a vital reaction, specifically hyperemia or ecchymoses (bruising) along the edges of the groove.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Area of hyperemia and ecchymoses along the edges of the groove is a definite ante-mortem sign and its presence must be confirmed by histology.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Explain the cardiac outcome of carotid sinus stimulation during manual strangulation (throttling).
back:
- Triggers strong parasympathetic stimulation.
- Results in bradycardia, decreased myocardial contractility, and sudden reflex cardiac arrest.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Increased tension... precipitates strong parasympathetic stimulation and produces inhibitory circulatory effects such as slowing of pulse... and sudden arrest of the heart.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the typical anatomical level of the ligature mark in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
- Hanging: High up, usually above the thyroid cartilage.
- Strangulation: Lower down, typically at the middle of the neck.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Site - Hanging: High up in the neck. Strangulation: Middle of neck.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Describe the depth variation of the ligature groove in hanging cases.
back: - The depth is not uniform. It is deepest at the point opposite the knot and becomes shallower toward the knot.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [depth of the groove is not uniform being deepest at a point opposite to the knot and gradually becoming shallower towards it.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Compare the incidence of hyoid bone fractures in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
- Hanging: Rare (only 3-5% of cases).
- Strangulation/Throttling: Very common finding due to direct manual pressure or ligature constriction.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Fracture of hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage is a rare finding occurring only in about 3-5% cases.] Page 154 (Book Page): [Hyoid bone usually and thyroid cartilage occasionally is fractured (in strangulation).]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Why do petechial hemorrhages (Tardieu’s spots) form in fatal asphyxia?
back:
- Anoxia causes capillary dilatation and increased wall permeability.
- Intravascular pressure rises, leading to capillary rupture and small focal blood leaks.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [Anoxia also increases permeability of capillary wall forcing fluid out into the tissue spaces... Capillaries eventually rupture causing blood leaks of small size... these petechial hemorrhages were noticed first by Tardieu.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Which anatomical feature distinguishes manual strangulation from ligature strangulation on external exam?
back: - Presence of crescentic nail marks and finger-tip bruises on the skin of the neck.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck (in throttling).]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the continuity of the ligature mark in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: In-continuous (absent at the knot site).
• Strangulation: Usually continuous all around the neck.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Hanging: Incomplete; Strangulation: Complete]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: How does the direction of the ligature mark differ between hanging and strangulation?
back:
• Hanging: Oblique (directed upward toward the knot).
• Strangulation: Horizontal/Transverse across the neck.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Hanging: Oblique; Strangulation: Horizontal]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Differentiate the primary constricting force in hanging and strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: Indirect force (applied through the weight of the body).
• Strangulation: Direct force applied to the ligature.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [Hanging: constricting force being applied indirectly through weight of the body. ... Strangulation: constricting force being applied directly to ligature.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Scenario: A body presents with a horizontal ligature mark in the middle of the neck. Diagnosis?
back:
• Diagnosis: Strangulation.
• Hanging marks are typically high up (above thyroid cartilage) and oblique.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Hanging: High up in the neck; Strangulation: Middle of neck]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the severity of facial congestion in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: Usually mild or absent facial congestion.
• Strangulation: Marked and intense facial congestion.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Hanging: Mild or absent; Strangulation: Marked]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: What is the defining feature of the groove's depth in a hanging ligature mark?
back: • Depth is non-uniform; it is deepest opposite the knot and becomes shallower toward it.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [depth of the groove is not uniform being deepest at a point opposite to the knot and gradually becoming shallower towards it.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: How do petechial hemorrhages compare between hanging and strangulation?
back:
• Hanging: Scanty petechial hemorrhages.
• Strangulation: Intense and profuse petechial hemorrhages.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Hanging: Scanty; Strangulation: Intense]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Does the presence of fingernail marks on the neck help differentiate these conditions?
back: • Yes. Absent in hanging; often present (parallel or vertical) in strangulation due to struggle.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Hanging: Absent; Strangulation: Present (parallel or vertical above ligature mark)]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the incidence of Hyoid bone fractures in hanging and strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: Rare (roughly 3-5%).
• Strangulation: Much more common, often involving the Hyoid or Thyroid cartilage.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Hanging: Rare finding occurring only in about 3-5% cases. ... Strangulation: Hyoid bone usually and thyroid cartilage occasionally is fractured.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Where is the typical position of the knot in classic hanging?
back: • Occipital region (back of the head). In strangulation, the knot is usually in front.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Hanging: occipital side; Strangulation: In front of neck]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Define Shajjah-i-Hashimah under the Qisas and Diyat Ordinance.
back:
- Refers to the fracturing of a bone without displacement.
- Specifically applies to injuries located on the head or face.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Hashimah: Fracturing of bone withoutt displacement.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Explain the mechanical causation of a greenstick fracture in forensic pediatrics.
back:
- Occurs because children's bones are more elastic than adults.
- Mechanical force causes damage to only one side of the bone near the point of impact.
citation: Page 60 (Book Page): [Long bones of children are comparatively more elastic and show less damage to only one side of bone close to application of force resulting in green stick fracture.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Differentiate between Shajjah-i-Hashimah and Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah.
back:
- Hashimah: Fracture of the bone without displacement.
- Munaqqilah: Fracture of the bone with displacement.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Hashimah: Fracturing of bone withoutt displacement. Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah: Fracturing of bone with displacement.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: A victim presents with a skull fracture where the wound touches the brain membranes. Classify this hurt.
back:
- It is classified as Shajjah-i-Ammah.
- This is a specific legal category for head injuries involving the cranial cavity.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Ammah: Fracturing of bone and the wound touching the membranes of brain.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: What are the medico-legal consequences of failing to X-ray a suspected fracture?
back:
- It is categorized as civil negligence.
- The medical practitioner may be sued in civil court for compensation due to lack of professional carefulness.
citation: Page 24 (Book Page): [Civil negligence results from lack of carefulness during medical treatment and common examples are... failure to X-ray a fractured bone... Such cases are brought before a civil court for decision of award of compensation in terms of money.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Define Shajjah-i-Damighah regarding its diagnostic criteria.
back:
- Characterized by the fracturing of a bone.
- Must involve the rupturing of the brain membranes (meninges).
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Damighah: Fracturing of bone with rupturing of the brain membranes.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Describe the medico-legal significance of flaking bone fractures in a burnt corpse.
back:
- They are postmortem artifacts caused by intense heat.
- They must be differentiated from ante-mortem mechanical trauma to avoid false allegations of assault.
citation: Page 64 (Book Page): [Postmortem artifact which are produced during fire needs recognition and they are flaking bone fracture & protein coagulation...]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Contrast local deformation versus general deformation in skull fracture mechanics.
back:
- Local: Impact causes crushing/bending at the site (e.g., depressed fracture).
- General: Compression causes the skull to bulge and fracture at distant, weaker points (e.g., fissured fracture).
citation: Page 61 (Book Page): [Local deformation at the site occurs, if the force applied is sufficient to cause crushing... General deformation of whole skull occurs due to compression of the skull... producing fractures in these planes... usually fissured ones occurring at parts of skull distant from actual site.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: Why is the supporting bony tissue of teeth highly significant in mass disaster identification?
back:
- It is characteristic to the individual and indestructible by fire.
- It withstands decomposition better than other soft tissues, providing a permanent record.
citation: Page 48 (Book Page): [Teeth supporting bony tissues are characteristic to an individual, indestructible in fire and also withstand decomposition... their importance have been enhanced... in cases of mass disasters.]

category: Explain medico-legal importance of fracture of bone/tooth
front: Q: What is the primary medico-legal importance of identifying a fracture in a traffic accident?
back:
- Determines the 'Extent of Damage' (Moderate/Severe/Fatal).
- Essential for assessing legal responsibility and calculating Arsh or Daman compensation.
citation: Page 86 (Book Page): [Extent of damage to injured... Moderate (injuries serious, victim hospitalized for a week); Severe (injuries endanger life)... Page 27 (Book Page): Shajjah... Fracture of bone...]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the anatomical direction of the ligature mark in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: Oblique (usually directed upward toward the knot).
• Strangulation: Horizontal and transverse across the neck.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [Hanging] Direction of the mark is oblique going upward towards the knot... [Strangulation] directed transversely across it.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Why is the ligature mark typically 'in-continuous' in hanging cases?
back:
• The suspension force pulls the ligature away from the skin at the knot.
• This leaves a physical gap in the impression opposite the primary weight-bearing side.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [Hanging] characteristic is that it is in-continuous and absent at the place against knot.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Differentiate the typical level of the ligature mark on the neck in these two acts.
back:
• Hanging: High up, situated above the thyroid cartilage.
• Strangulation: Lower down, usually at the middle of the neck or below the thyroid cartilage.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [Hanging] usually situated in upper part of the neck above thyroid cartilage... [Strangulation] place is over the lower part of the larynx and upper part of the trachea.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: A corpse presents with a neck groove of uniform depth all around. Identify the mechanism.
back:
• Strangulation.
• Hanging grooves are deepest opposite the knot and shallow toward it; strangulation depth is consistent due to direct force.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [Hanging] depth of the groove is not uniform being deepest at a point opposite to the knot... [Strangulation] horizontal and continuous ligature mark of uniform depth all around neck.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: What is the primary histological/gross step to differentiate ante-mortem from post-mortem ligature marks?
back:
• Inspection for vital reaction.
• Check for hyperemia and ecchymoses along the edges of the groove.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): Presence of vital reaction to the skin and deeper tissues... Area of hyperemia and ecchymoses along the edges of the groove is a definite ante-mortem sign.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Where is the knot imprint typically found in a 'Typical Hanging' case?
back:
• At the occipital region.
• In atypical hanging, it is usually located at the side of the face or chin.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): In typical hanging, ligature knot is at occipital region whereas in atypical mostly at side of face.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the presence of fingernail marks on the neck in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: Usually absent.
• Strangulation: Often present (parallel or vertical) above or below the ligature mark due to struggle.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page) Table 13.3: [Nail marks] Hanging: Absent. Strangulation: Present (parallel or vertical above ligature mark).

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Compare the incidence of hyoid bone fractures in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: Rare (approximately 3-5%).
• Strangulation: Common/Frequent due to direct, forceful pressure against the vertebrae.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Hanging] Fracture of hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage is a rare finding occurring only in about 3-5% cases... [Strangulation] Hyoid bone usually and thyroid cartilage occasionally is fractured.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: How does internal soft tissue damage compare in these two neck constrictions?
back:
• Hanging: Minimal bruising of neck muscles and connective tissue.
• Strangulation: Extensive/Significant bruising of fascia, muscle sheaths, and muscles.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Hanging] degree of bruising of connective tissue and muscles... [Strangulation] Internal damage is bruising of soft tissues of neck such as fascia, muscle sheaths, muscles.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the typical facial appearance (congestion/cyanosis) in hanging and strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: Minimal/Absent if complete; visceral congestion is not marked.
• Strangulation: Intense cyanosis, marked facial congestion, and numerous petechial hemorrhages.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page) Table 13.3: [Cyanosis/Congestion] Hanging: Nil or absent. Strangulation: Intense and Marked.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the continuity of the ligature mark in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
- Hanging: In-continuous (absent at the knot site).
- Strangulation: Continuous (encircles the neck completely).
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [Hanging] ligature mark. It characteristic is that it is in-continuous and absent at the place against knot. Page 153 (Book Page): [Strangulation mark] It is all around the neck, directed transversely across it.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Compare the typical direction of the neck mark in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
- Hanging: Oblique (directed upward towards the knot).
- Strangulation: Horizontal or transverse.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [Hanging] Direction of the mark is oblique going upward towards the knot. Page 153 (Book Page): [Strangulation] directed transversely across it.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Differentiate the anatomical level of the ligature mark between these two conditions.
back:
- Hanging: High up, usually above the thyroid cartilage.
- Strangulation: Lower down, typically in the middle of the neck.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3] Hanging: High up in the neck. Strangulation: Middle of neck.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: A corpse presents with a horizontal neck mark of uniform depth. Diagnose the mechanism.
back:
- Ligature Strangulation.
- Hanging presents with non-uniform depth that decreases towards the knot.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3] Hanging: Depth of the groove Decreases towards knot. Strangulation: Uniform.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the mechanism of constricting force in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
- Hanging: Indirect force (body weight).
- Strangulation: Direct force applied to the ligature.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): Hanging... constricting force being applied indirectly through weight of the body. Page 153 (Book Page): strangulation... constricting force being applied directly to ligature.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Compare the intensity of facial cyanosis and petechiae in hanging and strangulation.
back:
- Hanging: Usually less marked or minimal.
- Strangulation: Intense cyanosis and marked petechial hemorrhages.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3] Hanging: Cyanosis: Nil or absent... Petechaeal hemorrhage: Scanty. Strangulation: Intense... marked.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Distinguish the occurrence of neck structure fractures in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
- Hanging: Rare (approx. 3-5%).
- Strangulation: Common (Hyoid bone usually and thyroid cartilage occasionally fractured).
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Hanging] Fracture of hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage is a rare finding occurring only in about 3-5% cases. Page 153 (Book Page): [Strangulation] Hyoid bone usually and thyroid cartilage occasionally is fractured.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Identify the significance of 'Saliva dribbling' in a suspected hanging case.
back:
- Diagnostic of ante-mortem hanging.
- Results from pressure on salivary glands while alive.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): Dribbling of saliva from the corner of the mouth in hanging is a sure sign of ante-mortem hanging.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Differentiate the typical knot position in 'Typical Hanging' from atypical presentations.
back:
- Typical: Knot is at the occipital region.
- Atypical: Knot is at any other site (e.g., side of face).
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): in typical hanging, ligature knot is at occipital region whereas in atypical mostly at side of face.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: List the external features of the neck mark in 'Manual Strangulation' (Throttling).
back:
- Bruises from finger-tips.
- Adjacent vertical or parallel nail marks.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Throttling] Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the typical direction of the ligature mark in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
* Hanging: Oblique, directed upward toward the knot.
* Strangulation: Horizontal and transverse across the neck.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page)-153: [Direction of the mark is oblique going upward towards the knot... directed transversely across it.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Why are asphyxial signs (cyanosis, congestion) more intense in strangulation than in hanging?
back: Strangulation involves direct, continuous force causing immediate venous and arterial occlusion. Hanging often involves partial or gradual compression due to body weight suspension.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Intensity of cyanosis, visceral congestion and petechaeal hemorrhages is marked... In hanging... Visceral congestion and petechaeal hemorrhages are not marked.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Differentiate the continuity of the ligature mark in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
* Hanging: In-continuous (absent at the knot site).
* Strangulation: Usually continuous, completely encircling the neck.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page)-153: [characteristic is that it is in-continuous and absent at the place against knot... It is all around the neck.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: A body presents with a horizontal ligature mark below the thyroid cartilage. Identify the likely cause.
back: Homicidal strangulation. Hanging marks are typically oblique and situated high in the neck, usually above the thyroid cartilage.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [hanging... usually situated in upper part of the neck above thyroid cartilage... strangulation... place is over the lower part of the larynx.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Compare the incidence of hyoid bone fractures in hanging versus homicidal strangulation.
back:
* Hanging: Rare (approx. 3-5%).
* Strangulation: Common, resulting from direct transverse pressure against the cervical vertebrae.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Hyoid bone usually and thyroid cartilage occasionally is fractured... In hanging... rare finding occurring only in about 3-5% cases.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Describe how the depth of the ligature groove typically varies in hanging.
back: The groove is non-uniform; it is deepest opposite the knot and becomes progressively shallower as it approaches the knot.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [depth of the groove is not uniform being deepest at a point opposite to the knot and gradually becoming shallower towards it.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Which specific finding confirms that a hanging ligature mark was produced ante-mortem?
back: Presence of a vital reaction, specifically a line of hyperemia or ecchymosis (bruising) along the edges of the groove.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Area of hyperemia and ecchymoses along the edges of the groove is a definite ante-mortem sign.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: What external neck findings differentiate manual strangulation (throttling) from ligature strangulation?
back: Manual strangulation (throttling) shows bruising from fingertips and parallel or crescentic fingernail marks rather than a continuous linear groove.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic... in middle of neck.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: In hanging, what mechanism explains rapid death occurring without typical asphyxial features?
back: Vagal inhibition (reflex cardiac arrest) caused by stimulation/pressure on the carotid sinus or vagus nerve.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [Mechanism of death in hanging includes... reflex cardiac arrest... through pressure over carotid sinus.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Which specific external fluid sign is pathognomonic for ante-mortem hanging?
back: Saliva dribbling from the corner of the mouth (opposite the knot), caused by direct pressure on the salivary glands.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Dribbling of saliva... is a definite ante-mortem sign and its presence can be relied upon.]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the direction of the ligature mark in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
- Hanging: Oblique, directed upward toward the knot.
- Strangulation: Horizontal and transverse across the neck.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3] Hanging: Oblique. Strangulation: Horizontal.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: What primary mechanism causes death in typical hanging compared to strangulation?
back:
- Hanging: Cerebral anoxia due to jugular/carotid compression and reflex cardiac arrest.
- Strangulation: Combined cerebral anoxia and intense respiratory obstruction (asphyxia).
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): Mechanism of death in hanging includes cerebral anoxia... asphyxia by lifting of glottis... Page 154 (Book Page): Mechanism of death [in strangulation] is cerebral anoxia due to external pressure.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Differentiate the continuity of the ligature mark between hanging and strangulation.
back:
- Hanging: Incomplete/Interrupted (absent at the knot site).
- Strangulation: Complete and continuous (all around the neck).
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3] Hanging: Incomplete. Strangulation: Complete.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: A corpse has intense facial congestion and vertical nail marks; which condition is indicated?
back:
- Strangulation (Throttling).
- Hanging typically shows pale or less marked congestion, whereas strangulation presents marked cyanosis and struggle marks.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3] Facial congestion: Mild or absent [in hanging]... Marked [in strangulation]. Nail marks: Absent... Present.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: How is a vital reaction confirmed at the site of a ligature mark?
back:
- Presence of hyperemia and ecchymoses (bruising) along the edges of the groove.
- This distinguishes ante-mortem injuries from post-mortem artifacts.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): Area of hyperemia and ecchymoses along the edges of the groove is a definite ante-mortem sign.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Compare the typical anatomical height of ligature marks in both conditions.
back:
- Hanging: High up in the neck (above thyroid cartilage).
- Strangulation: Middle or lower part of the neck (often below thyroid cartilage).
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3] Site: High up in the neck [Hanging]. Middle of neck [Strangulation].

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Why are Tardieu's spots more prominent in strangulation than in hanging?
back:
- Strangulation involves a higher degree of violent respiratory struggle and venous obstruction.
- Hanging (especially typical) may involve rapid death by cardiac inhibition.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3] Petechaeal hemorrhage: Scanty [in hanging]... Immense [in strangulation].

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the occurrence of hyoid bone fractures in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
- Hanging: Rare (only 3-5% of cases).
- Strangulation: Common, especially greater cornua of hyoid and thyroid cartilage superior horns.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): Fracture of hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage is a rare finding [in hanging] occurring only in about 3-5% cases. Page 153 (Book Page): [Strangulation] Hyoid bone usually and thyroid cartilage occasionally is fractured.

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: How does the depth of the ligature groove differ along its circumference in hanging?
back:
- In hanging, depth decreases as it approaches the knot (deepest opposite the knot).
- In strangulation, depth is usually uniform all around.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3] Depth of the groove: Decreases towards knot [Hanging]. Uniform [Strangulation].

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Where is the knot imprint usually located in homicidal strangulation?
back:
- Usually in front of the neck.
- In typical hanging, the knot is located on the occipital (back) side.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3] Knot: On back of neck [Hanging]. In front of neck [Strangulation].

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the anatomical site of the ligature mark in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: High up in the neck, typically above the thyroid cartilage.
• Strangulation: Middle or lower neck, usually over the larynx or upper trachea.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Hanging: High up in the neck... Strangulation: Middle of neck]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Differentiate the direction of the ligature mark in hanging and strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: Oblique, directed upward toward the position of the knot.
• Strangulation: Horizontal and transverse across the neck.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Hanging: Oblique... Strangulation: Horizontal]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the continuity of the ligature mark in hanging versus strangulation cases.
back:
• Hanging: Incomplete or in-continuous; absent at the point corresponding to the knot.
• Strangulation: Complete and continuous all around the neck.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Hanging: Incomplete... Strangulation: Complete]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: How does the depth of the ligature groove vary in hanging compared to strangulation?
back:
• Hanging: Non-uniform; deepest opposite the knot, becoming shallower towards it.
• Strangulation: Uniform depth throughout the entire circumference of the mark.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Hanging: Decreases towards knot... Strangulation: Uniform]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the typical position of the ligature knot in hanging and strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: Usually situated at the back (occipital region) or side of the face.
• Strangulation: Usually firmly tied in the front of the neck.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Hanging: on back of neck... Strangulation: In front of neck]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Compare the intensity of facial cyanosis and congestion between hanging and strangulation.
back:
• Hanging: Mild or absent.
• Strangulation: Intense cyanosis and marked facial congestion.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Hanging: Nil or absent... Strangulation: Intense]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
front: Q: Contrast the frequency of hyoid bone fractures in hanging versus strangulation deaths.
back:
• Hanging: Rare (occurring in only about 3-5% of cases).
• Strangulation: Hyoid bone is usually fractured.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Fracture of hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage is a rare finding occurring only in about 3-5% cases. ... Hyoid bone usually ... is fractured (in strangulation)]

category: Differentiate between ligature marks due to hanging and strangulation
