• Mechanisms: Cerebral anoxia (external pressure on windpipe) or reflex cardiac asystole (carotid sinus stimulation).
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Manual strangulation (throttling) is constriction of neck, of a person by other person with one or both hands... Mechanism of death is cerebral anoxia due to external pressure on windpipe from front and sides. Reflex cardiac asystole takes place due to variations of tension within carotid sinuses.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Describe the physiological response to increased tension in the carotid sinus during throttling.
back:
• Precipitates strong parasympathetic stimulation.
• Inhibitory effects: Slowing of pulse, depressed myocardial contractility/conductivity, and generalized vasodilation, leading to circulatory failure.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Increased tension... precipitates strong parasympathetic stimulation and produces inhibitory circulatory effects such as slowing of pulse, depression of myocardial contractility and conductivity and generalized vasodilatation.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What are the characteristic external skin findings on the neck in a throttling victim?
back:
• Bruises from pressure of finger-tips (often crescentic).
• Adjacent fingernail marks (scratches) typically located on the front or sides of the neck.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Contrast the asphyxial features above the constriction site in manual strangulation.
back:
• Acute facial congestion and deep cyanosis.
• Prominent petechial hemorrhages (Tardieu's spots) in the skin and conjunctivae.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Amongst general pathological changes, facial congestion, cyanosis and petechayae hemorrhages are prominent, usually seen in areas above level of constriction.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Which deep neck structures are typically bruised internally in throttling?
back:
• Neck fascia and muscle sheaths.
• Muscles and retro-pharyngeal tissue (due to compression against the spine).
• Occasionally the base of the tongue.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Adjacent neck soft tissues under skin such as fascia, muscle sheet, muscles and retropharyngeal tissue also get bruised due to pressure against spine. In severe cases, base of the tongue may also be bruised.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Identify the most common laryngeal skeletal fractures in manual strangulation.
back:
• Fracture of the hyoid bone (greater cornua).
• Fracture of the thyroid cartilage (specifically the superior horns).
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [Other specific finding is fracture of thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone.] Page 150 (Book Page): [Common sites are greater cornue of hyoid bone and superior horn of thyroid cartilage especially when gets calcified as in advanced age.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: How does a forensic examiner differentiate between a direct blow to the neck and manual pressure?
back:
• Fracture of the body of the hyoid or thyroid cartilage suggests a direct blow (e.g., karate).
• Throttling typically fractures the greater cornua or superior horns via compression.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Common sites are greater cornue of hyoid bone and superior horn... fracture of body of hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage generally follows a direct blow like in karate.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What is the only reliable corroborative finding in a putrefied body suspected of throttling?
back:
• Fractures of the hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage.
• Soft tissue bruises (external and internal) are usually masked or destroyed by decomposition.
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [Decomposition may present difficulties in the recognition of both external as well as internal bruises... In putrefied body, this is the only corroborative finding.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What physiological chain results if throttling causes decreased tension in the carotid sinus?
back:
• Strong sympatho-adrenal stimulation.
• Results: Accelerated pulse, increased myocardial contractility, and generalized vasoconstriction with rising blood pressure.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Decreased tension produces strong sympatho-adrenal stimulation accelerating rate of pulse and increase in myocardial contractility, conductibility and generalized vaso-constriction with rise in blood pressure.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What autopsy technique is required to prevent artifactual neck bruising during dissection?
back:
• Complete drainage of blood must be achieved first.
• This is done by removing the contents of the head and chest before exploring the neck layers.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Precaution that no seepage of blood from vessels occurs into surrounding tissue... advised complete drainage of blood by first removing contents of head and chest before neck dissection.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What specific external neck marks characterize manual strangulation (throttling)?
back:
* Finger-tip bruises (circular/oval contusions)
* Finger-nail marks (crescentic or linear scratches)
* Usually located on the front or sides of the neck.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Explain the physiological mechanism of sudden death via 'vagal inhibition' in throttling.
back:
* Pressure on the carotid sinus or vagus nerve
* Triggers strong parasympathetic stimulation
* Causes sudden cardiac asystole (arrest) and circulatory failure.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Sudden sympatho-adrenal or parasympathetic stimulation leads to circulatory failure, which proves fatal... Reflex cardiac asystole takes place due to variations of tension within carotid sinuses.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Contrast the incidence of laryngeal fractures in throttling versus hanging.
back:
* Throttling: High incidence; diagnostic hallmark (fractured hyoid/thyroid cartilage)
* Hanging: Very rare (3-5%) due to indirect force application.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Fracture of hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage is a rare finding occurring only in about 3-3% cases.] Page 155 (Book Page): [Diagnosis of throttling will heavily depend upon presence of fracture of thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: A body presents with intense facial cyanosis and crescentic scratches on the larynx. Most likely diagnosis?
back:
* Homicidal manual strangulation (Throttling)
* Asphyxial signs (cyanosis, Tardieu's spots) are typically very prominent in this mode.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Manual strangulation (throttling) is constriction of neck... with one or both hands... facial congestion, cyanosis and petechiaeal hemorrhages are prominent.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Which specific neck structures are commonly bruised internally during a throttling autopsy?
back:
* Sternocleidomastoid muscles
* Deep neck fascia and muscle sheaths
* Retropharyngeal soft tissues
* Occasionally the base of the tongue.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Adjacent neck soft tissues under skin such as fascia, muscle sheet, muscles and retropharyngeal tissue also get bruised due to pressure against spine.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What are 'Tardieu's spots' and where are they most visible internally?
back:
* Petechial hemorrhages from capillary rupture
* Result of anoxic damage and venous stasis
* Most visible under serous coverings of organs (lungs/heart).
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [These petechial hemorrhages were noticed first by Tardieu... occur in the substance of the organs, but are more readily seen under their serous coverings.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Why is total blood drainage required before neck dissection in suspected throttling cases?
back:
* To prevent 'seepage' artifacts
* Prevents blood leaking from cut vessels into tissues, which mimics ante-mortem bruising.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Precaution that no seepage of blood from blood vessels occurs into surrounding tissue spaces causing artifact bruising... advised complete drainage of blood from head and chest before neck dissection.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Differentiate the effects of carotid artery versus jugular vein compression in the neck.
back:
* Carotid Compression: Cerebral anoxia and rapid unconsciousness
* Jugular Compression: Venous congestion and petechial hemorrhages in the head/face.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Carotid artery, which reduces arterial blood supply... Jugular vein, which affects venous return from head producing congestion and hemorrhage in tissues above level of constriction.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Define 'Mugging' as a variant of mechanical asphyxia.
back:
* Manual strangulation performed with the bend of the elbow
* May also involve pressure from a foot or knee to the neck.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Mugging is compression of the neck of the victim with bend of elbow or by applying a foot or knee to the neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: How is the 'vital reaction' identified at the site of neck injuries in throttling?
back:
* Presence of hyperemia (redness)
* Microscopic infiltration of white blood cells (after 4-6 hours)
* Effused blood within the tissue spaces.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Evidence of vital reaction to the skin and deeper tissues in relation to ligature mark will point to ante-mortem occurrence. Area of hyperemia and bruising... can be confirmed by histology.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: What is the medical definition of manual strangulation (throttling)?
back: Constriction of the neck by another person using one or both hands.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Manual strangulation (throttling) is constriction of neck of a person by other person with one or both hands.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Describe the primary mechanisms of death in cases of manual strangulation.
back:
• Cerebral anoxia (vessel occlusion).
• Reflex cardiac asystole (carotid sinus stimulation).
• Asphyxia (airway obstruction).
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Mechanism of death is cerebral anoxia due to external pressure on windpipe from front and sides. Reflex cardiac asystole takes place due to variations of tension within carotid sinuses.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: How do fingernail marks in throttling typically appear and differ from ligature marks?
back: Characterized as crescentic abrasions often associated with finger pad bruises; unlike hanging, they lack a continuous circular groove.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: A body shows crescentic abrasions on the neck and thyroid cartilage fracture. Identify the manner of death.
back: Homicidal (Throttling). Suicide by manual strangulation is physically impossible.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Manual strangulation (throttling) is... homicide following sexual assault are common occurrence.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Explain how carotid sinus stimulation during throttling leads to immediate circulatory failure.
back: Increased tension triggers strong parasympathetic stimulation (vagus nerve), causing slowing pulse, myocardial depression, and sudden cardiac arrest.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Increased tension precipitates strong parasympathetic stimulation and produces inhibitory circulatory effects such as slowing of pulse, depression of myocardial contractility... leading to circulatory failure.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Which two internal neck structures are classically fractured during throttling?
back:
• Hyoid bone (greater cornua).
• Thyroid cartilage (superior horns).
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [Diagnosis of throttling will mainly depend upon presence of fracture of thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Where are petechial hemorrhages most prominently distributed in a victim of throttling?
back: Specifically in areas above the level of constriction, including the face, conjunctivae, and neck skin.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Amongst general pathological findings, facial congestion, cyanosis and petechial hemorrhages are prominent, usually seen in areas above level of constriction.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Why is internal neck dissection critical in decomposed bodies suspected of manual strangulation?
back: Decomposition masks external bruises/nail marks; internal fractures of the hyoid or thyroid structures persist as the only reliable diagnostic clues.
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [Decomposition may present difficulties in the recognition of both external as well as internal bruises and diagnosis of throttling will mainly depend upon presence of fracture of thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Explain the role of stagnant circulation in producing facial cyanosis during throttling.
back: Occlusion of jugular veins prevents blood return from the head, causing capillary engorgement, deoxygenation, and deep blue coloration.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Cerebral anoxia occurs due to occlusion of blood vessels... causes stagnation of circulation producing anoxia... facial congestion, cyanosis and petechial hemorrhages are prominent.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: List the internal soft tissue findings characteristic of manual strangulation.
back:
• Bruising of neck muscles (fascia/muscle sheaths).
• Retropharyngeal tissue bruising.
• Occasional tearing of blood vessels.
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [Adjacent neck soft tissues under skin such as fascia, muscle sheet, muscles and retropharyngeal tissue also get bruised due to pressure.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Describe the characteristic external appearance of fingertip bruises in a throttling victim.
back: Circular or oval bruises (6-10 mm) caused by pressure. Typically found on the front or sides of the neck.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What is the mechanism behind reflex cardiac arrest during manual strangulation?
back: Manual pressure or variations in tension within the carotid sinuses stimulates the vagus nerve, precipitating sudden circulatory failure.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Reflex cardiac asystole takes place due to variations of tension within carotid sinuses... Stimulates vagus nerve precipitating cardiac arrest.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Compare the incidence of hyoid bone fractures in throttling versus hanging.
back: Hyoid fractures are common in throttling (manual strangulation) but rare (3-5%) in hanging victims.
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [Hyoid bone usually and thyroid cartilage occasionally is fractured (in strangulation).] Page 153 (Book Page): [Fracture of hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage is a rare finding occurring only in about 3-5% cases (in hanging).]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: How is throttling diagnosed in a decomposed body where soft tissue bruises are invisible?
back: Diagnosis relies on identifying fractures of the hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage, which resist putrefaction longer than soft tissues.
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [Decomposition may present difficulties... diagnosis of throttling will finally depend upon presence of fracture of thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: List the specific internal neck soft tissues likely to show bruising in manual strangulation.
back: Subcutaneous fascia, muscle sheaths, and muscles (including retropharyngeal tissues) due to compression against the spinal column.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Adjacent neck soft tissues under skin such as fascia, muscle sheet, muscles and retropharyngeal tissue also get bruised due to pressure against spine.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What is 'Mugging' and which part of the body is used as the constricting force?
back: A form of manual strangulation using the bend of the elbow, knee, or foot to compress the victim's neck.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Mugging is compression of the neck of the victim with bend of elbow or by applying a foot or knee to the neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What specific internal finding is observed at the base of the tongue in throttling?
back: Bruising of the tongue base due to the larynx being forcefully lifted and the tongue pushed upward and backward.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [In severe cases, base of the tongue may also be bruised.] Page 150 (Book Page): [Usual mechanism is for larynx to be lifted up so that tongue blocks back of the throat.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: A suspect claims neck marks are postmortem. How does 'vital reaction' disprove this in throttling?
back: True ante-mortem throttling shows tissue hyperemia, cellular infiltration (after 4-6 hours), and hemorrhages within the deep neck muscles.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Observation of vital reaction to the skin and deeper tissues in relation to ligature mark will point to the occurrence... Area of hyperemia and bruising.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Describe the recommended autopsy technique for blood-free neck dissection in throttling cases.
back: Drain all blood by removing head and chest contents first; then use a wide primary incision for layer-wise muscle exploration.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Prinslo and Gordon recommended wider primary incision of neck... advised complete drainage of blood before removing contents of head and chest before neck dissection.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Which specific laryngeal structures are most prone to fracture in elderly throttling victims?
back: Greater cornua of the hyoid bone and the superior horn of the thyroid cartilage, particularly when calcified.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Common sites of fractures are greater cornua of hyoid bone and superior horn of thyroid cartilage especially when calcified as in advanced age.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What is the typical morphology and location of bruises found in manual throttling?
back:
- Characterized as circular or oval fingertip bruises.
- Primarily situated on the front or both sides of the neck.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Explain the mechanism and specific site of hyoid bone fracture in manual throttling.
back:
- Mechanism: Manual compression forces bone against cervical vertebrae.
- Specific Site: Fractures occur at the greater cornua.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Common sites of fracture are greater cornue of hyoid bone... producing in addition injuries to related soft tissues.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Contrast the intensity of facial cyanosis and petechiae in throttling versus hanging.
back:
- Throttling: Intense and marked due to efficient venous obstruction and prolonged struggle.
- Hanging: Usually less marked or scanty.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [In throttling, intensity of cyanosis, visceral congestion and petechacal hemorrhages is marked, usually seen in areas above level of constriction.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: In cases of throttling by soft mediums, what internal findings confirm the diagnosis?
back:
- Fracture of thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone.
- Bruising of deep neck muscles and retro-pharyngeal tissues.
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [Decomposition may present difficulties... and diagnosis of throttling will mainly depend upon presence of fracture of thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What internal findings are expected in the air passages of a throttled victim?
back:
- Mucosal congestion and edema of the larynx and trachea.
- Presence of blood-stained frothy mucus in the lumen.
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [Laryngeal injury gives rise to difficulty in swallowing... and tracheal findings include blood-stained frothy mucus.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: How do fingernail marks typically appear in manual throttling?
back:
- Appear as crescentic or linear abrasions (scratches).
- Located immediately adjacent to fingertip bruises.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Which specific deep tissue is often bruised in throttling due to pressure against the spine?
back:
- The retro-pharyngeal tissue.
- Underlying fascia and muscle sheaths of the neck.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Adjacent neck soft tissues under skin such as fascia, muscle sheet, muscles and retropharyngeal tissue also get bruised due to pressure against spine.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Why might an autopsy be 'negative' in a suspected case of manual neck compression?
back:
- Death occurred via reflex cardiac arrest (vagal inhibition).
- Stimulation of the carotid sinus or vagus nerve causes immediate death before asphyxial signs develop.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Sudden sympatho-adrenal or parasympathetic stimulation leads to circulatory failure... Deaths occurring by such mechanisms are usually very rapid.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Describe the significance of thyroid cartilage fractures in throttling autopsies.
back:
- Specifically involves the superior horns.
- Highly indicative of manual throttling, especially when calcified in older adults.
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [Recognition of fracture of thyroid structures is of great value in diagnosis of throttling.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What is the primary anatomical finding in the tongue during a throttling autopsy?
back:
- Bruising at the base of the tongue.
- Internal protrusion of the tongue blocking the pharynx.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [In severe cases, base of the tongue may also be bruised... larynx to be lifted up so that tongue blocks back of the throat.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What are the characteristic external skin marks found on the neck in manual throttling?
back:
1. Bruises from finger-tip pressure.
2. Adjacent fingernail marks (scratches).
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Describe the mechanism of reflex cardiac asystole triggered during manual neck compression.
back: Increased tension in the carotid sinus precipitates strong parasympathetic stimulation, causing inhibitory effects like slowing of pulse and cardiac arrest.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Increased tension occurs either by occlusion of the carotid artery above the sinus or by application of pressure on the carotid sinus. Increased tension precipitates strong parasympathetic stimulation and produces inhibitory circulatory effects such as slowing of pulse... and cardiac arrest.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Contrast the intensity of general asphyxial signs in throttling compared to hanging.
back: Throttling shows marked intensity of facial congestion, cyanosis, and petechial hemorrhages due to significant venous return obstruction.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Amongst general pathological changes, facial congestion, cyanosis and petechaeal hemorrhages are prominent, usually seen in areas above level of constriction.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: In a decomposed body, which internal findings remain most reliable to confirm a diagnosis of throttling?
back: Fractures of the laryngeal structures (hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage), as they persist longer than soft tissue findings.
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [Decomposition may present difficulties in the recognition of both external as well as internal bruises and diagnosis of throttling will mainly depend upon presence of fracture of thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What anatomical step must be performed to visualize internal injuries to the larynx in throttling?
back: Layer-wise dissection of neck muscles and detailed examination of the thyroid gland and trachea.
citation: Page 151 (Book Page): [In suspected interference of neck, layer-wise dissection of the neck muscles should be done and detailed examination of each muscle, thyroid gland, larynx and trachea must also be undertaken.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: List the specific deep soft tissues in the neck typically bruised during manual strangulation.
back:
1. Fascia and muscle sheaths.
2. Retropharyngeal tissue.
3. Base of the tongue.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Adjacent neck soft tissues under skin such as fascia, muscle sheet, muscles and retropharyngeal tissue also get bruised due to pressure against spine... base of the tongue may also be bruised.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What is the significance of applying bilateral traction during the inspection of natural orifices in strangulation cases?
back: It ensures proper and good exposure of body openings and clefts (oral, anal, or vulvar) to locate evidence of violation.
citation: Page 118 (Book Page): [Lateral traction is applied for proper and good exposure of body openings and clefts... best inspects vulvar and anal openings.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: How is artefactual bruising in the neck muscles avoided during autopsy in suspected throttling cases?
back: By ensuring complete drainage of blood from the head and chest before performing the neck dissection.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Medical examiner is advised complete drainage of blood by first removing contents of head and chest before neck dissection... to avoid seepage of blood from blood vessels into surrounding tissue.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Explain the physiological outcome of decreased tension on the carotid sinus during throttling.
back: Strong sympatho-adrenal stimulation, leading to tachycardia, increased myocardial contractility, and generalized vaso-constriction.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Decrease tension occurs due to application of pressure on carotid artery below the sinus. Decreased tension produces strong sympatho-adrenal stimulation accelerating rate of pulse... and generalized vaso-constriction.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: State the two mechanisms that cause fractures of the laryngeal structures in throttling.
back:
1. Direct pressure on the bone.
2. Indirect pressure transmitted through the thyro-hyoid ligament.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Larynx... fractures by two mechanisms; direct pressure on bone and indirect pressure through thyro-hyoid ligament.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What is the formal definition of manual strangulation or throttling?
back: Constriction of a person's neck by another individual using one or both hands.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Manual strangulation (throttling) is constriction of neck of a person by other person with one or both hands.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What are the two primary pathophysiological mechanisms of death in throttling?
back:
1. Cerebral anoxia from external pressure on windpipe/vessels.
2. Reflex cardiac asystole from carotid sinus tension variations.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Mechanism of death is cerebral anoxia due to external pressure on windpipe from front and sides. Reflex cardiac asystole takes place due to variations of tension within carotid sinuses.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Contrast the distribution of petechial hemorrhages in throttling versus general asphyxia.
back: They are prominent and usually localized in areas above the level of neck constriction.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Amongst general pathological changes facial congestion, cyanosis and petechaeal hemorrhages are prominent, usually seen in areas above level of constriction.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: A victim presents with crescentic nail marks on the neck. What is the likely diagnosis?
back: Manual strangulation (throttling), as finger-tip bruises and adjacent nail marks on the front/sides of the neck are characteristic.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both side of the neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: How does increased tension on the carotid sinus during throttling cause sudden death?
back: It triggers strong parasympathetic stimulation, leading to inhibitory effects like pulse slowing and depressed myocardial conductivity.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Increased tension... precipitates strong parasympathetic stimulation and produces inhibitory circulatory effects such as slowing of pulse, depression of myocardial contractility and conductivity.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: List the common internal neck skeletal structures fractured during manual strangulation.
back: The thyroid cartilage and the hyoid bone.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Adjacent neck soft tissues... also get bruised due to pressure against spine along with fractures of laryngeal structures.] Page 155 (Book Page): [diagnosis of throttling will mainly depend upon presence of fracture of thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Which internal soft tissues are typically bruised during manual neck compression?
back:
1. Fascia and muscle sheets.
2. Neck muscles.
3. Retro-pharyngeal tissue.
4. Base of the tongue.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Adjacent neck soft tissues under skin such as fascia, muscle sheet, muscles and retropharyngeal tissue also get bruised... base of the tongue may also be bruised.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: In a decomposed body, what remains the only reliable finding for a diagnosis of throttling?
back: Fractures of the thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone, as soft tissue bruises may be obscured.
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [Decomposition may present difficulties in the recognition of both external as well as internal bruises and diagnosis of throttling will mainly depend upon presence of fracture of thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What happens to the brain during the stagnation of circulation in manual strangulation?
back: Occlusion of neck arteries and veins causes cerebral anoxia, progressing to coma and death.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Cerebral anoxia occurs due to occlusion of blood vessels supplying blood to the brain. Compression of arteries and veins causes stagnation of circulation producing anoxia, coma and death.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Define the variant of manual strangulation known as "mugging."
back: Neck compression using the bend of the elbow or the application of a foot or knee.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Mugging is compression of the neck of the victim with bend of elbow or by applying a foot or knee to the neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Define throttling (manual strangulation) based on the method of constriction?
back:
• Constriction of the neck using one or both hands.
• A form of homicidal mechanical asphyxia.
• Force is applied directly to the windpipe and neck vessels.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Manual strangulation (throttling) is constriction of neck of a person by other person with one or both hands.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What are the two primary pathophysiological mechanisms of death in manual strangulation?
back:
• Cerebral anoxia: Due to occlusion of neck vessels and windpipe.
• Reflex cardiac asystole: Precipitated by carotid sinus stimulation via the vagus nerve.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Mechanism of death is cerebral anoxia due to external pressure on windpipe from front and sides. Reflex cardiac asystole takes place due to variations of tension within carotid sinuses.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Describe the characteristic external 'nail marks' found during an autopsy for throttling.
back:
• Characteristic crescent-shaped abrasions.
• Located on the front or sides of the neck.
• Usually found adjacent to finger-tip bruises.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Case: A body is in an advanced state of decomposition. Which skeletal finding supports throttling?
back:
• Fracture of the hyoid bone.
• Fracture of the thyroid cartilage.
• These skeletal injuries resist putrefaction better than soft tissue bruises.
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [Decomposition may present difficulties in the recognition of both external as well as internal bruises and diagnosis of throttling will mainly depend upon presence of fracture of thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: How does increased tension on the carotid sinus during throttling lead to sudden death?
back:
• Causes strong parasympathetic stimulation.
• Leads to slowed pulse, decreased myocardial contractility, and generalized vasodilation.
• Results in rapid circulatory failure.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Increased tension... Precipitates strong parasympathetic stimulation and produces inhibitory circulatory effects such as slowing of pulse, depression of myocardial contractility and conductivity and generalized vasodilatation.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: List the specific external facial findings associated with manual strangulation.
back:
• Intense cyanosis (blue discoloration).
• Acute facial congestion.
• Profuse petechial hemorrhages (Tardieu's spots), especially on cheeks and conjunctivae.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Amongst general pathological changes, facial congestion, cyanosis and petechaeal hemorrhages are prominent, usually seen in areas above level of constriction.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What internal soft tissue neck injuries are specifically noted during a throttling autopsy?
back:
• Bruising of the fascia and muscle sheaths.
• Bruising of retropharyngeal tissue.
• Bruising of the base of the tongue.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Adjacent neck soft tissues under skin such as fascia, muscle sheet, muscles and retropharyngeal tissue also get bruised... In severe cases, base of the tongue may also be bruised.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: How is 'seepage' artifact differentiated from ante-mortem bruising during neck dissection?
back:
• Use the 'Prinsloo and Gordon' technique.
• Drain blood by removing head and chest contents first.
• Ante-mortem bruises remain, while seepage artifacts are avoided.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Precaution that no seepage of blood from blood vessels occurs into surrounding tissue spaces... Prinslo and Gordon recommended complete drainage of blood from the neck by removing contents of head and chest before neck dissection.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What anatomical structures are most vulnerable to direct pressure in elderly victims of throttling?
back:
• Greater cornua of the hyoid bone.
• Superior horn of the thyroid cartilage.
• Increased risk due to age-related calcification.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Common sites of fractures are greater cornue of hyoid bone and superior horn of thyroid cartilage especially when calcified as in advanced age.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What is the typical gross appearance of finger-tip bruises on a victim's neck?
back:
• Small, circular, or oval bruises.
• Patterned according to finger placement.
• Located specifically on the front or sides of the neck.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips... are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What three external facial signs are most prominent in a victim of manual strangulation?
back:
1. Intense facial congestion.
2. Deep cyanosis.
3. Profuse petechial hemorrhages (Tardieu's spots) on the face and conjunctivae.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Amongst general pathological changes, facial congestion, cyanosis and petechaeal hemorrhages are prominent, usually seen in areas above level of constriction.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Describe the mechanism of reflex cardiac arrest triggered during throttling.
back: Manual pressure on the carotid sinus increases tension, triggering strong parasympathetic stimulation. This leads to pulse slowing, myocardial depression, and sudden circulatory failure.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Reflex cardiac asystole takes place due to variations of tension within carotid sinuses: Increase tension ... precipitates strong parasympathetic stimulation and produces inhibitory circulatory effects such as slowing of pulse, depression of myocardial contractility and conductivity ... leading to circulatory failure.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What is the forensic significance of crescentic abrasions on the neck during autopsy?
back: They represent fingernail marks from an assailant's hand, typically found adjacent to fingertip bruises on the front or sides of the neck.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: In a suspected throttling case, why must the brain be removed before neck dissection?
back: To ensure complete drainage of blood from the neck, preventing artifactual bruising that may be misinterpreted as ante-mortem trauma.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Prinslo and Gordon recommended ... complete drainage of blood by first removing contents of head and chest before neck dissection.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Which specific laryngeal structures are most frequently fractured in manual strangulation?
back:
1. Greater cornua of the hyoid bone.
2. Superior horns of the thyroid cartilage (especially in older, calcified subjects).
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Common sites of fractures are greater cornue of hyoid bone and superior horn of thyroid cartilage especially when calcified as in advanced age.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Identify the characteristic internal soft tissue findings of the neck in throttling.
back:
1. Bruising of neck fascia and muscle sheaths.
2. Contusion of retro-pharyngeal tissue.
3. Occasional bruising at the base of the tongue.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Adjacent neck soft tissues under skin such as fascia, muscle sheet, muscles and retropharyngeal tissue also get bruised ... In severe cases, base of the tongue may also be bruised.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: How does the positioning of the larynx contribute to death in throttling?
back: Mechanical pressure lifts the larynx, forcing the base of the tongue against the back of the pharynx, which completely blocks the airway.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Usual mechanism is for larynx to be lifted up so that tongue blocks back of the throat.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Why are laryngeal fractures valuable findings in a putrefied body suspected of throttling?
back: Hard structures like the hyoid and thyroid cartilage resist the decomposition that liquefies and obscures soft tissue bruising.
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [Decomposition may present difficulties ... and diagnosis of throttling will finally depend upon presence of fracture of thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone. In putrefied body, this is only corroborative finding.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Contrast the cardiovascular response between pressure applied above and below the carotid sinus.
back: Pressure above/at sinus: Parasympathetic stimulation (bradycardia/asystole). Pressure below: Sympatho-adrenal stimulation (tachycardia/hypertension).
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Increased tension ... precipitates strong parasympathetic stimulation ... Decreased tension produces strong sympatho-adrenal stimulation accelerating rate of pulse and increase in myocardial contractility...]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What internal hemorrhage finding in the neck is specific to manual strangulation?
back: Bruising caused by finger-tips pressing the soft tissues against the cervical vertebrae, often including deep muscular contusions.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Adjacent neck soft tissues under skin ... also get bruised due to pressure against spine along with fractures of laryngeal structures.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: How does ligature mark direction help determine the relative position of the knot?
back:
- Hanging: Oblique mark, directed upward toward the knot.
- Strangulation: Horizontal mark, usually continuous around the neck.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Hanging... Direction of the mark is oblique going upward towards the knot... Strangulation... directed transversely across it.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Describe the mechanism of 'garroting' regarding the assailant's position.
back:
- Assailant attacks from behind.
- Ligature is passed over the head and pulled tight to compress the neck against vertebrae.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [garroting in which victim is attacked from behind. A piece of rope... is passed over head placed in front of the neck and pulled.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: What external marks on the neck identify the assailant's hand placement in throttling?
back:
- Bruises from finger-tips (circular/oval).
- Linear nail marks adjacent to bruises.
- Usually found on the front or sides of the neck.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: In a homicidal cutthroat, where is the wound typically positioned compared to a suicidal one?
back:
- Homicidal: Boldly placed in the middle or lower neck.
- Suicidal: Usually high up on the neck, often on the side opposite the working hand.
citation: Page 80 (Book Page): [Suicidal... usually high up on left side in right handed person... Homicidal... is boldly placed in the center or in the middle.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: A victim has bruising in the bend of the elbow; what assailant technique does this suggest?
back:
- Suggests 'mugging.'
- Assailant compresses the neck using the crook of the arm, knee, or foot.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Mugging is compression of the neck of the victim with bend of elbow or by applying a foot or knee to the neck.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: How is wound depth used to differentiate between a self-inflicted and homicidal cutthroat?
back:
- Suicidal: Maximum depth at the initiation point.
- Homicidal: Maximum depth in the center/middle of the wound.
citation: Page 80 (Book Page): [Depth of wound... Suicidal... Maximum at the point of initiation... Homicidal... Maximum in the middle.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: What does the absence of 'hesitation cuts' suggest about the nature of a neck wound?
back:
- Strongly suggests homicide (assault).
- Suicidal wounds typically feature multiple superficial cuts near the main initiation point.
citation: Page 80 (Book Page): [Hesitation cut... Suicidal... Near initiation point... Assault... Absent.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: In cases of throttling, how does the presence of nail marks help identify the struggle?
back:
- Indicates manual compression by an assailant.
- Marks are typically vertical or parallel, found above the site of pressure or on the front of the neck.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Nail marks... Present (parallel or vertical above ligature mark)... in cases of throttling.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Define the 'tailing' of a wound and its significance in determining the assailant's hand use.
back:
- Tailing is a superficial extension of the wound.
- In suicide, tailing is found on the side of the working hand.
citation: Page 80 (Book Page): [Tailing... Suicidal... Present on working hand side... Assault... Absent.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: How does the level of the neck constriction help differentiate hanging from strangulation?
back:
- Hanging: Usually high up, above the thyroid cartilage.
- Strangulation: Usually lower down, at or below the thyroid cartilage.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Site... Hanging... High up in the neck... Strangulation... Middle of neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Define manual strangulation (throttling) and its primary causative force.
back:
* Constriction of the neck by one or both hands.
* The constricting force is applied directly by human hands.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Manual strangulation (throttling) is constriction of neck of a person by other person with one or both hands... constricting force being applied directly to ligature (note: text context implies direct hand force for manual).]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: How are the larynx and tongue displaced to obstruct the airway during throttling?
back:
* The larynx is lifted upward.
* The base of the tongue is pushed backward against the pharynx, blocking air entry.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Usual mechanism is for larynx to be lifted up so that tongue blocks back of the throat.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Contrast external skin findings with deep internal findings in manual strangulation.
back:
* External: Fingertip bruises with adjacent crescentic nail marks on the neck.
* Internal: Bruising of neck fascia, muscle sheaths, and retropharyngeal tissues.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Specific findings depend upon method... Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic... Adjacent neck soft tissues under skin such as fascia, muscle sheet, muscles and retropharyngeal tissue also get bruised.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Case: A victim is compressed via the bend of an elbow. Name this variant.
back:
* Mugging.
* It is a specific form of throttling involving the forearm or knee.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Mugging is compression at the neck of the victim with bend of elbow or by applying a foot or knee to the neck.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Why are cyanosis and facial petechiae typically more intense in throttling than hanging?
back:
* Caused by jugular vein occlusion.
* Prevents venous return while arterial supply may partially continue, causing extreme capillary engorgement and rupture.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Jugular vein, which affects venous return from head producing congestion and hemorrhage in tissues above level of constriction.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: State the classical facial distribution of Tardieu's spots in mechanical neck compression.
back:
* Skin of the face.
* Conjunctivae and eyelids.
* Often accompanied by facial cyanosis and congestion.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Petechaeal hemorrhages are on face and conjunctivae. Specific local findings... are bruising of the skin, mucosa of nose and lips.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: Describe the proper neck dissection technique to avoid postmortem artifacts in throttling.
back:
* Layer-wise dissection of neck muscles.
* Complete drainage of blood by removing head/chest contents first to prevent 'seepage' artifacts.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Dissection of neck in such cases is ruled by consideration of thorough exploration... advised complete drainage of blood from the neck by removing contents of head and chest before neck dissection.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: In a putrefied body, what autopsy finding remains a reliable indicator of manual strangulation?
back:
* Fractures of laryngeal structures (hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage).
* These hard skeletal elements persist despite soft tissue decomposition.
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [Decomposition may present difficulties in the recognition of both external as well as internal bruises... diagnosis of throttling will primarily depend upon presence of fracture of thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: How does carotid artery occlusion contribute to the mechanism of death in throttling?
back:
* Causes cerebral anoxia.
* Constriction reduces arterial blood supply, leading to rapid brain hypoxia and unconsciousness.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Cerebral anoxia occurs due to occlusion of blood vessels supplying blood to the brain... producing anoxia, coma and death.]

category: Identify external and internal autopsy findings of death due to throttling
front: Q: What specific mucosal internal finding is characteristic of violent throttling at the tongue?
back:
* Bruising at the base of the tongue.
* Caused by forceful pressure pushing the larynx and tongue against the spine.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [In severe cases, base of the tongue may also be bruised.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: What does a horizontal, continuous ligature mark of uniform depth imply about the manner of death?
back:
* Indicates homicidal strangulation.
* Suggests force was applied directly by an assailant standing in front of or behind the victim.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [horizontal and continuous ligature mark of uniform depth all around neck... constricting force being applied directly to ligature. Homicidal cases are common.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: How do fingernail marks on the neck help determine the assailant's hand position during throttling?
back: * A group of crescentic marks on one side with a thumb bruise on the other indicates a single-handed grip from the front.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Contrast the initiation site of neck wounds in suicidal vs. homicidal cutthroats regarding assailant position.
back:
* Suicidal: Initiated on the side opposite the working hand.
* Homicidal: Usually boldly placed in the center or consistent with the victim's position during assault.
citation: Page 80 (Book Page): [Table 7.5: Suicidal: Opposite side of working hand. Homicidal: Usually boldly placed in the center of the middle.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: A victim presents with diffuse bruising and a 'mugging' injury; what part of the assailant caused this?
back: * The bend of the elbow, a foot, or a knee was applied to the neck to compress the airway.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Mugging is compression of the neck of the victim with bend of elbow or by applying a foot or knee to the neck.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: What does the absence of a ligature mark at the 'knot' area indicate during a hanging investigation?
back: * It represents the point where the ligature was pulled upward and away from the neck by the weight of the body.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [characteristic is that it is in-continuous and absent at the place against knot. Direction of the mark is oblique going upward towards the knot.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: How does the verticality of 'hesitation cuts' on the neck suggest the manner of wounding?
back: * They are superficial, parallel marks near the initiation point, identifying the victim as the own assailant (suicide).
citation: Page 80 (Book Page): [Table 7.5: Suicidal: Hesitation cut near initiation point. Homicidal: Absent.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Where is the assailant typically positioned during 'garroting'?
back: * The assailant attacks from behind, passing a rope or flexible branch around the victim's neck to compress it against the vertebrae.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Special form of strangulation is garroting in which victim is attacked from behind. A piece of rope... is passed over head placed in front of the neck and pulled against the vertebrae.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: A victim shows fingernail marks high and horizontal above a ligature; what does this indicate?
back: * Indicates the victim attempted to pull the ligature away from the neck (defense struggle against an assailant).
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Table 13.3: Strangulation: Nail marks Present (parallel and vertical above ligature mark).]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Why are fractures of the hyoid bone rare in typical suicidal hanging compared to throttling?
back: * Hanging involves oblique traction; Throttling involves direct, forceful manual compression of the larynx and hyoid.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Fracture of hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage is a rare finding occurring only in about 3-5% cases.] Page 155 (Book Page): [Fracture of thyroid cartilage or hyoid bone... of great value in diagnosis of throttling.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: What does an 'atypical' hanging knot position reveal about the victim's final position?
back: * Atypical knots (side of face) often occur in partial hangings where the victim is not fully suspended off the ground.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [In typical hanging, ligature knot is at occipital region whereas in atypical mostly at side of face.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Contrast the ligature mark direction in homicidal strangulation versus suicidal hanging.
back:
* Strangulation: Mark is horizontal, continuous, and situated in the middle/lower neck.
* Hanging: Mark is oblique, discontinuous, and high up above the thyroid cartilage.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [In strangulation] It is all around the neck, directed transversely across it... [In hanging] Direction of the mark is oblique going upward towards the knot... usually situated in upper part of the neck above thyroid cartilage.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Describe the relative positions of the assailant and victim in cases of Garroting.
back:
* Assailant: Attacks from behind.
* Method: A ligature or flexible branch is passed over the head, placed in front of the neck, and pulled against the vertebrae.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Garroting] in which victim is attacked from behind. A piece of rope, wire or even a flexible branch of a tree is passed over head placed in front of the neck and pulled against the vertebrae.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: How do external neck marks indicate the assailant's position during manual throttling?
back:
* Marks: Bruises from finger-tips and adjacent nail marks indicate approach.
* Position: Marks on the front or sides of the neck reveal if the assailant used one or both hands from the front or behind.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck... reveal if the assailant used one or both hands... from front or behind.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Identify the attack type and assailant position when neck compression occurs via 'bend of elbow'.
back:
* Type: Mugging.
* Position: The assailant is typically positioned behind or to the side of the victim, applying pressure with the elbow or knee.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Mugging is compression of the neck of the victim with bend of elbow or by applying a foot or knee to the neck.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Why is the ligature mark in hanging discontinuous, and what does this signify?
back:
* Significance: The mark is absent at the knot site.
* Indication: This indicates the position of the suspension point relative to the body's gravity, differentiating it from the continuous marks of strangulation.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [Ligature mark... is in-continuous and absent at the place against knot. Direction of the mark is oblique going upward towards the knot.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: At what anatomical level is a homicidal strangulation mark typically found compared to hanging?
back:
* Strangulation: Lower part of the larynx or upper part of the trachea.
* Hanging: Usually above the thyroid cartilage.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [In strangulation] usual place is over the lower part of the larynx and upper part of the trachea. It is all around the neck, directed transversely across it.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: How does the depth of a hanging ligature groove help determine the point of suspension?
back:
* Rule: The groove is deepest opposite the knot.
* Progression: It becomes shallower as it approaches the suspension point (the knot), where the mark often disappears.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [Ligature mark... well-defined groove... depth of the groove is not uniform being deepest at a point opposite to the knot and gradually becoming shallower towards it.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Contrast the wound position in homicidal versus suicidal cut-throat injuries.
back:
* Suicidal: Usually high up on the neck, often on the side opposite the working hand.
* Homicidal: Boldly placed in the center of the middle or lower neck.
citation: Page 80 (Book Page): [Suicidal] Usually high up on left... [Homicidal] Is boldly placed in the center and in the middle.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Pressure on which neck structure during throttling indicates an assailant's attempt to cause reflex arrest?
back:
* Structure: Carotid sinus.
* Mechanism: Assailant pressure stimulates the vagus nerve, leading to sudden parasympathetic circulatory failure/cardiac asystole.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Manual strangulation] Sudden sympatho-adrenal or parasympathetic stimulation leads to circulatory failure... stimulation of the heart through abnormal stimulation of regulatory nerves as in carotid-sinus inhibition.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Describe the typical orientation of nail marks on the neck in manual throttling.
back:
* Orientation: Vertical or parallel.
* Significance: They are found adjacent to finger-tip bruises on the front or sides of the neck, indicating the assailant's grip.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Manual strangulation] Nail marks: Present (parallel or vertical above ligature mark) [Note: Referring to throttling marks in Table 13.3 and Page 154 (Book Page) text].]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: How does the ligature mark direction help identify the point of suspension in hanging?
back: The mark is directed obliquely and runs upward towards the knot, which reveals the point where the body was suspended.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [Direction of the mark is oblique going upward towards the knot. It is an imprint abrasion usually situated in upper part of the neck above thyroid cartilage.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: What does an 'in-continuous' mark on the neck indicate about the victim-ligature relationship?
back: It indicates hanging; the mark is absent at the knot position because the weight of the body pulls the ligature away from the skin at that point.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [characteristic is that it is in-continuous and absent at the place against knot.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Contrast the level of neck marks in hanging versus homicidal strangulation.
back: Hanging marks are usually high up (above thyroid cartilage). Strangulation marks are typically horizontal and located in the middle of the neck.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page) Table: [Site: High up in the neck (Hanging); Middle of neck (Strangulation). Direction: Oblique (Hanging); Horizontal (Strangulation).]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: How do fingernail marks on the victim's neck reveal the assailant's method in throttling?
back: Thumb imprints on one side and multiple finger marks on the opposite side indicate single-handed throttling and the assailant's orientation.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks... present in front or both sides of the neck. Specific findings depend upon method of throttling whether with one hand or both hands.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: In garroting, how does the assailant's position relate to the resulting marks on the victim?
back: The assailant attacks from behind; the ligature is pulled backward, producing a horizontal, continuous mark typically against the vertebrae.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [garroting in which victim is attacked from behind. A piece of rope... is passed over head placed in front of the neck and pulled from back.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: What does a uniform depth in a horizontal ligature mark suggest about the assailant's force?
back: It indicates ligature strangulation, where the assailant applied force directly and evenly with a cord, unlike the varying depth seen in hanging.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page) Table: [Depth of the groove: Decreases towards knot (Hanging); Uniform (Strangulation).]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: How do vertical nail scratches above a ligature mark characterize the victim-assailant struggle?
back: These are defense marks made by the victim's own nails while attempting to pull away the assailant’s ligature during strangulation.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page) Table: [Nail marks: Absent (Hanging); Present (parallel or vertical above ligature mark) (Strangulation).]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Identify the mark indicating an assailant used the 'mugging' technique on a victim.
back: Broad, ill-defined bruising in the bend of the elbow or across the neck, often without the distinct fingertip marks of manual throttling.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Mugging is compression of the neck of the victim with bend of elbow or by applying a foot or knee to the neck.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Why is the deepest part of a hanging groove significant for locating the suspension point?
back: The groove is deepest at the point opposite the knot, helping to deduce exactly where the knot/point of suspension was relative to the body.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [depth of the groove is not uniform being deepest at a point opposite to the knot and gradually becoming shallower towards it.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: What does the absence of nail marks on the neck suggest in a suspected homicidal hanging?
back: It suggests hanging, where death is caused by body weight alone; their presence usually points to manual strangulation or a struggle with an assailant.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page) Table: [Nail marks: Absent (Hanging); Present (Strangulation).]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: How is the assailant's position identified during a "Garroting" attack?
back:
* Assailant attacks from behind.
* Rope is passed over the head, placed in front of the neck, and pulled across toward the vertebrae.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [In garroting] victim is attacked from behind. A piece of rope, cord or even a flexible branch of a tree is passed over head placed in front of the neck and pulled across passage against the vertebrae.

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: What external neck marks specifically suggest the assailant used manual strangulation (throttling)?
back:
* Bruises from finger-tips.
* Adjacent crescentic nail marks.
* Located characteristic in the front or both sides of the neck.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [In throttling] Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck.

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Contrast the knot position in Typical versus Atypical hanging suspension.
back:
* Typical: Knot is located at the occipital region (back of head).
* Atypical: Knot is mostly at the side of the face or chin.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): In typical hanging, ligature knot is at occipital region whereas in atypical mostly at side of face.

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: How do neck marks in homicidal cutthroat differ from suicidal attempts?
back:
* Homicidal: Wound is boldly placed in the center or middle neck; structures cut equally on both sides.
* Suicidal: High up, usually starting on the side opposite the working hand.
citation: Page 180 (Book Page): [Table 7.5] Homicidal cutthroat: Boldly placed in the center, in the middle... Neck structures: Equally cut on both sides. Suicidal: Opposite side of working hand.

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: What does a ligature knot firmly tied in front of the neck suggest?
back:
* Strongly indicates homicidal strangulation.
* Contrast: Hanging knots are usually posterior or lateral.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): Ligature is retained in position in homicidal cases with knot usually firmly tied in front.

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Define the external method and mark location in "Mugging" assaults.
back:
* Compression of neck with the bend of the elbow.
* Pressure applied via the assailant's foot or knee.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): Mugging is compression at the neck of the victim with bend of elbow or by applying a foot or knee to the neck.

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Where is the ligature mark typically situated in homicidal strangulation versus hanging?
back:
* Strangulation: Middle of neck, below thyroid cartilage.
* Hanging: Upper neck, usually above the thyroid cartilage.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Strangulation] mark... is usually situated at any part of the neck but commonest place is over the lower part of the larynx and upper part of the trachea.

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: How can a single-handed throttling grip be determined from external neck bruises?
back:
* Thumb mark: Large bruise on one side.
* Finger marks: Several smaller bruises on the opposite side.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips... [suggesting] method of throttling whether with one hand or both hands.

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: What physiological event causes instant death during manual neck compression without asphyxial signs?
back:
* Reflex cardiac arrest.
* Triggered by mechanical stimulation of the carotid sinus or vagus nerve.
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): Reflex cardiac asystole takes place due to variations of tension within carotid sinuses... Sudden sympatho-adrenal or parasympathetic stimulation leads to circulatory failure.

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Which specific laryngeal structures are most vulnerable to fracture during homicidal throttling?
back:
* Greater cornua of the hyoid bone.
* Superior horn of the thyroid cartilage (especially in calcified older victims).
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): Common sites of fractures are greater cornue of hyoid bone and superior horn of thyroid cartilage especially when calcified as in advanced age.

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Contrast the direction of the neck mark in hanging versus ligature strangulation.
back:
- Hanging: Oblique, directed upward toward the knot.
- Ligature Strangulation: Horizontal and transverse across the neck.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [direction of the mark is oblique going upward towards the knot] Page 153 (Book Page): [directed transversely across it.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: How do the edges of a moving abrasion (graze) indicate the assailant's force direction?
back: - The epidermis heaps or piles up at the far end of the force application.
citation: Page 54 (Book Page): [Moving abrasion indicates direction of abrasive force, showing heaping of piling up of the epidermis on the far end.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Differentiate the point of maximum wound depth in suicidal versus homicidal cut-throat.
back:
- Suicidal: Deepest at the point of initiation.
- Homicidal: Deepest in the middle of the neck.
citation: Page 80 (Book Page): [Suicidal... Depth is more at the point of initiation... Homicidal... maximum depth in the middle.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: A victim presents with four circular bruises on the left neck and one on the right. Interpret this.
back:
- Throttling (Manual Strangulation).
- Assailant used the right hand from the front (four fingers on left neck, thumb on right).
citation: Page 154 (Book Page): [Bruises due to pressure of finger-tips having adjacent nail marks are characteristic and present in front or both sides of the neck.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: What does a gap in a neck ligature mark indicate regarding the assailant's setup?
back: - The gap (in-continuity) marks the exact position of the knot where the loop was pulled away.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [characteristic is that it is in-continuous and absent at the place against knot.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: What defines 'Garroting' in terms of the relative positions of the assailant and victim?
back:
- Assailant attacks from behind.
- A ligature is thrown over the head and pulled tight against the vertebrae.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): [Type of strangulation is garroting in which victim is attacked from behind... pulled across the vertebral passage against the vertebrae.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: How is the 'working hand' identified in self-inflicted neck injuries?
back:
- Tailing of the wound occurs toward the working hand.
- Hesitation cuts are usually on the side of initiation (opposite working hand).
citation: Page 79 (Book Page): [They show tailing towards working hand] Page 80 (Book Page): [Hesitation cuts at point of initiation... Present on working hand side]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Contrast the anatomical level of the mark in hanging versus strangulation.
back:
- Hanging: Upper neck (above thyroid cartilage).
- Ligature Strangulation: Lower neck (over larynx or trachea).
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): [situated in upper part of the neck above thyroid cartilage.] Page 153 (Book Page): [usual place is over the lower part of the larynx and upper part of the trachea.]

category: Determine the position of assailant and victim from external marks on neck
front: Q: Describe 'Mugging' in terms of mechanical neck constriction technique.
back: - Constriction using the bend of the elbow or the knee against the victim's neck.
